tldr: The unconditional contribution consists of three proved pieces: common-ray Foelner operators are path-independent and have explicit translation-boundary ratios; Carter's bounded-ratio kernels give fixed-base compact multinomial transfer with separately displayed semantic, covariance, and \(C_{2/\kappa}m\log(m)/\sqrt n\) charges; and compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit together with two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows, but no global upper limit. Replayable moving-offset transfer and CertGluePFL termination remain conditional on a separately supplied finite compatibility package satisfying the five certificates listed in the open-ended question.

project_justification.gap: Carter's bounded-ratio comparison controls fixed positive-cell multinomial experiments on compact parameter sets, but it neither supplies finite recession families nor controls a seam escaping every compact set. Moving offsets additionally require compact-offset arrangement stability and separately supplied envelopes for replayable accounting. At recession, common-ray commutativity does not control the Gaussian discrepancy between every incident candidate on simultaneous collars. The unresolved effective-compatible-density question asks whether canonical sections and every positive-weight candidate can be certified safe, translated tails can be bounded uniformly, and a finite rational schedule can make the accumulated compatibility ledger tend to zero.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification inference combines discontinuous completed labels, intersecting unbounded recession faces, and a global honesty constraint. Equality on a geometric face does not control all candidates mixed on nearby simultaneous collars, while compact local asymptotics cannot detect a hard seam escaping to infinity. The proved compact/windowed theory and the unanswered compatibility-density question at unbounded recession seams are therefore mathematically distinct.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves common-ray operator coherence, Carter-based fixed-base compact transfer with separate semantic and covariance terms, a global minimax lower limit, and two-sided convergence on diagonally selected expanding lawful windows. It does not prove global effective compatible density. The corresponding open-ended question lists the five certificates still required. Replayable moving-offset rules and CertGluePFL termination are asserted only under an affirmative answer or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.

related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) supplies the bounded-ratio comparison between fixed positive-cell multinomial experiments and their matched multivariate normal experiments through parameter-independent kernels. The present paper separately accounts for score maps, covariance replacement, completed-affine-arrangement stability, moving offsets, and diagonally selected expanding lawful windows. Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013, Assumptions A--B and Proposition 1) motivate an always-employed wage comparison; the asserted embedding is restricted to the singleton-covariate, known rational assignment-floor, perfect-compliance, monotone-employment, finite-wage-grid submodel with positive always-employed mass, and gives neither unrestricted-class inclusion nor automatic sharpness transfer. Day and Markov--Kakutani invariant-mean theory and Namioka's 1964 Foelner conditions concern a single amenable commuting action and supply neither an input-computable modulus nor semantic coverage, separated-risk safety, translated-tail control, or branching-refinement complexity.
technical_internal_limitation: Effective compatible density is unresolved under the standing assumptions. One unproved obligation is to show that every canonical chart section remains in each required \(D_v\), \(H_r\), and declared chart-neighborhood incidence region. The remaining obligations are safety of every positive-weight candidate; exact overlap traces or a valid Gaussian-weighted face-cone discrepancy bound on simultaneous supports; translated-uniform guard and normal-base tails; and computed refinement counts \(N_j\) with schedules \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) for which every accumulated error vanishes and \(N_j/L_j\) tends to zero. No refinement-independent ledger constant is assumed. The four-label milliscale certificate and unconditional global CertGluePFL termination therefore remain unresolved.
honest_scope: The causal target is the same-law joint identified set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals; no Cartesian joint sharpness is claimed. Carter-backed sampled-data conclusions are fixed-compact or expanding-window statements. Compact exhaustion proves a global lower limit and two-sided windowed convergence, but neither a global limsup nor a globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal. The paper proves common-ray operator identities, Gaussian smoothing, one-chart averaging, and a telescoping inequality applicable once a finite family with certified edge discrepancies has already been supplied. It does not prove existence of finite families whose total compatibility ledger vanishes. Effective compatible density remains an open-ended question, and CertGluePFL termination and replayable global Gaussian certification remain conditional.
interpretation: The Gaussian experiment is the valid local decision target on each fixed lawful direction window. Carter's comparison gives unconditional qualitative fixed-compact and moving-offset transfer once the respective compact hypotheses hold; finite replayable Gaussian-rule construction remains conditional on effective compatible density or another sufficient compatibility package, and numerical replayability also requires separately supplied effective error envelopes. Compact exhaustion gives a global minimax lower limit and two-sided convergence only along diagonally selected expanding lawful windows; it gives neither a computable window selection nor a global upper limit. The common-ray library is an algebraically coherent recession representation, not a compatibility-density theorem.

definitions.construction: For every \(R_f\ge0\), action functional \(f:\mathcal A\to[0,R_f]\), mean cell \(C\), incidence edge \(e=(i,j)\), protected neighborhood \(P_{C,e}\), and path load \(g_{C,e}(w)=\sum_{k:e\in\pi_C(k)}\lambda_k(w)\), define \(F_i^f(w)=\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}f(A)q_{i,A}(w)\), take \(M_{C,f}=C\cap D_v\) for coverage of \(v\) and \(M_{C,f}=C\cap H_r\) for risk, and set \(\Gamma_{C,e}^f=\sup_{h\in M_{C,f}}[\int_{P_{C,e}}g_{C,e}|F_i^f-F_j^f|\phi_{\Sigma}(w-h)\,dw+R_f\int_{P_{C,e}^{c}}g_{C,e}\phi_{\Sigma}(w-h)\,dw]\). Define \(\rho_{\mathrm{led}}\) as the sum of all such terms, chart errors, \(R_f\omega(h)/2\), Gaussian tails, covariance enclosures, integration enclosures, and rational rounding errors.
inputs: a finite core and recession library
protected neighborhoods and outward integral enclosures

definitions.name: Exact full-set coverage repair
definitions.construction: If \(\widetilde K\) has global coverage at least \(1-\eta-\rho\), define \(\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho}(\widetilde K)\) to report \(V\) with probability \(\rho/(\eta+\rho)\) and otherwise draw from \(\widetilde K\).
inputs: a rule with a certified coverage deficit \(\rho\)

definitions.name: CertGluePFL search and certification handle
definitions.construction: Enumerate the finite classes \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\), exact rational incidence forests for the flattened nonempty components \(v,b\), their projection back to semantic labels \(v\), rational action probabilities, and finite rational atomic dual measures; enclose every weighted Gaussian integral outward; repair the best semantic-label primal exactly; and increase the core, chart, atom, cut, and precision indices according to the certified ledger until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\).

definitions.name: Legal always-selected-complier law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\{P:P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:known-assignment-probabilities},\text{ass:instrument-stratum-positivity},\text{ass:iv-randomization},\text{ass:treatment-consistency},\text{ass:selection-consistency},\text{ass:outcome-consistency},\text{ass:no-defiers},\text{ass:weak-selection-monotonicity},\text{ass:aggregate-target-positivity}\}\).

definitions.name: Selected-complier marginal-capacity outer map
definitions.construction: For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), compute \(c_{axk}(p)=(2a-1)\{p_{x,1,a,1,y_k}/\pi_1(x)-p_{x,0,a,1,y_k}/\pi_0(x)\}\), \(C_{ax}(j)=\sum_{k\le j}c_{axk}(p)\), \(q_{ax}=\sum_kc_{axk}(p)\), and \(m_x=\min\{q_{0x},q_{1x}\}\). Set \(L_{ax}(j)=[C_{ax}(j)-q_{ax}+m_x]_+\), \(U_{ax}(j)=\min\{m_x,C_{ax}(j)\}\), \(Q_a^{-}(t)=\min\{y_j:\sum_xU_{ax}(j)\ge tM_{\mathrm{ASC}}\}\), \(Q_a^{+}(t)=\min\{y_j:\sum_xL_{ax}(j)\ge tM_{\mathrm{ASC}}\}\), \(\underline\Delta^{\mathrm{out}}(t)=Q_1^{-}(t)-Q_0^{+}(t)\), and \(\overline\Delta^{\mathrm{out}}(t)=Q_1^{+}(t)-Q_0^{-}(t)\). These last two quantities are outer endpoints; the sharp effect endpoints are the separate optimizations over \(\mathcal F(p)\).
inputs: an observed multinomial law \(p\) induced by \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\)

definitions.name: Completed coordinatewise-endpoint label fan
definitions.construction: Use the fixed semantic assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\). Evaluate the complete rational branch and endpoint-program cut list at \(p_0\); freeze every nonzero base sign, retain only zero-base cuts with nonzero tangent normal \(B^{\prime}\alpha_{\psi}\), and treat zero tangent normals as fixed ties. Enumerate every incident weak completion of this active arrangement. For each semantic pattern \(v\), form the closed rational tangent cell \(P_{v,b}^0\), include equality faces in every incident cell, discard empty cells, and set \(D_v^0=\bigcup_bP_{v,b}^0\). Flatten \((v,b)\) only for recession computation and project honesty, actions, and loss back to \(v\).
inputs: the fixed Job Corps assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\)

definitions.name: Canonical semantic-separation radius certificate
definitions.construction: Run the total component and point selections defining \(i_*\) and \(u_*\). For every rival component, use the first violated rational row and a rational upper enclosure of its \(\Sigma_0\)-norm to compute \(\rho_{v,b}\), using zero if no row is violated. Set \(\rho_0\) to the minimum of these receipts and one, and set \(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\).
inputs: the completed rational tangent component geometry

definitions.name: Lawful causal multinomial local parameters
definitions.construction:
For each \(n\in\mathbb N\),
\[
 \mathcal U_n=\{u\in\mathbb R^d:p_n(u)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\}.
\]

definitions.name: Multinomial truth regions
definitions.construction: For each \(n\in\mathbb N\), enumerate the same legal branch completions after substituting \(p=p_n(u)\), form the closed cells \(P_{n,v,b}\) with every incident equality face retained and empty cells discarded, and define \(D_{n,v}=\bigcup_bP_{n,v,b}=\{u\in\mathcal U_n:v\in\Lambda[\vartheta_{\mathrm{ASC}}\{p_n(u)\}]\}\) and \(\mathcal V_n(u)=\{v\in V:u\in D_{n,v}\}\). The component index is computational; \(\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}\), \(H_{n,r_0}\), and \(M_n\) remain semantic-label objects.

definitions.name: Multinomial globally honest rule class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}=\{K_n:\inf_{v\in V}\inf_{u\in D_{n,v}}\Pr_{p_n(u)}\{v\in K_n(N_n)\}\ge1-\eta_0\}\) for each \(n\in\mathbb N\).

definitions.name: Multinomial separated risk domain
definitions.construction: \(H_{n,r_0}=\{u\in\mathcal U_n:\mathcal V_n(u)=\{v\},\ \inf_{v'\ne v}\inf_{g\in D_{n,v'}}\|u-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\ge r_0\}\) for each \(n\in\mathbb N\).
inputs: the multinomial truth regions and fixed local Gaussian metric

definitions.name: Multinomial honest separated minimax profile
definitions.construction: \(M_n=\inf_{K_n\in\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}}R_{n,r_0}(K_n)=\inf_{K_n\in\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}}\sup_{u\in H_{n,r_0}}E_{p_n(u)}[\ell_0\{K_n(N_n)\}]\) for each \(n\in\mathbb N\).

definitions.name: Recursive comparison and explicit moving-boundary handle
definitions.construction: Apply parameter-independent recursive binomial-to-normal Markov kernels on fixed positive-support strata. For the declared finite active list \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\), retain exactly \(\zeta_{n,j}(u)=c_{n,j}+a_j^{\prime}u+e_{n,j}(u)\), require limiting offsets to lie in \(\mathcal K_0\), deactivate a facet only when its displayed slack diverges to its feasible side, and charge localization at tolerance \(\tau\) by \(\mathfrak b_0(\tau)\). Localize the common transferred rule before compact exhaustion and add covariance, tail, comparison, and semantic-union diameter charges to the outward ledger.
inputs: a certified Gaussian rule for the relevant offset experiment
the explicitly declared local multinomial family \(p_n(u)\)

definitions.name: Four-label milliscale-refinement handle
definitions.construction: Start from the exhibited rule \(Q_{49/25}\), the exhibited atomic measures \(\beta_4,\nu_4\), and their exact scalar dual evaluation \(L_4\). Alternate rational recession-chart refinement, protected-neighborhood integration, primal cutting planes, and dual atom insertion while retaining a separately outward-rounded charge for every seam, tail, covariance, repair, and solver operation.

definitions.name: Full compatible-law fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F(p)=\{\widetilde P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}:\widetilde P(O=j)=p_j\ \forall j\in\mathcal J\}\), where membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) imposes every declared assignment, positivity, conditional-randomization, consistency and exclusion, compliance, selection-monotonicity, and target-mass restriction.

definitions.name: Finite response-type fiber polytope
definitions.construction: Enumerate \(\{\mathcal R_x:x\in\mathcal X\}\), assign weights \(\lambda_{xr}\ge0\) for \(r\in\mathcal R_x\), and define \(\Xi(p)\) by unit total mass, \(T_0\lambda=p\), stratum positivity, and always-selected-complier mass at least \(m_*\). Associate each feasible weight vector with the latent law that first draws \(X,R\) with masses \(\lambda_{xr}\), then draws \(Z\) from the known table and applies the declared consistency and exclusion maps.

definitions.name: Same-law joint quantile-effect identified set
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p)=\{\Delta_P:P\in\mathcal F(p)\}\), with \(\Delta_P(t)=Q_{1,P}(t)-Q_{0,P}(t)\) for every \(t\in\mathcal T\).

definitions.name: Lower same-law endpoint construction
definitions.construction: For fixed \((p,t)\), enumerate all pairs \((j_0,j_1)\) on \(\mathcal Y\). For each pair, impose in \(\Xi(p)\) the weak threshold inequalities at \(j_0,j_1\), introduce one common slack below \(t\) for every applicable predecessor inequality, and maximize that slack; declare the pair feasible exactly when the optimum is positive, with no predecessor constraint at \(j_a=1\). Choose a feasible pair minimizing \(y_{j_1}-y_{j_0}\), choose the lexicographically least basic maximizer of its positive-slack program, and let \(P_t^-(p)\) be the induced law.

definitions.name: Upper same-law endpoint construction
definitions.construction: For fixed \((p,t)\), enumerate all pairs \((j_0,j_1)\) on \(\mathcal Y\). For each pair, impose in \(\Xi(p)\) the weak threshold inequalities at \(j_0,j_1\), introduce one common slack below \(t\) for every applicable predecessor inequality, and maximize that slack; declare the pair feasible exactly when the optimum is positive, with no predecessor constraint at \(j_a=1\). Choose a feasible pair maximizing \(y_{j_1}-y_{j_0}\), choose the lexicographically least basic maximizer of its positive-slack program, and let \(P_t^+(p)\) be the induced law.

definitions.name: External compact polyhedral-label Gaussian experiments
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak E_K=\{(K_{\mathrm{par}},d,V,\{D_v^K=D_v\cap K_{\mathrm{par}}\}_{v\in V},\Sigma,\delta,\eta,r):\text{ass:compact-external-domain},\text{ass:compact-label-cover},\text{ass:rational-positive-covariance},\text{ass:compact-separated-domain-nonempty}\}\). Honesty, separated risk, and every parameter supremum are restricted to \(K_{\mathrm{par}}\).

definitions.name: Finite compatible moving-slack system
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\), use \(c_{n,j}=\sqrt n\,\psi_j\{p_n(0)\}\), \(a_j=B^{\prime}\alpha_j\), \(e_{n,j}(u)=\sqrt n[\psi_j\{p_n(u)\}-\psi_j\{p_n(0)\}]-a_j^{\prime}u\), and \(\zeta_{n,j}(u)=c_{n,j}+a_j^{\prime}u+e_{n,j}(u)\). Admissible finite limits satisfy \(c\in\mathcal K_0\), and localization at width \(\tau\) is charged by \(\mathfrak b_0(\tau)\).
inputs: the complete active cut list \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\)

definitions.name: Exhibited four-label facet rule
definitions.construction: Use the displayed matrices \(F_v\), whiten \(w=(a,b)\) to \(z=(a/\sqrt{1/8},b/\sqrt{3/20})\), and set \(Q_{49/25}(w)=\{v\in V_4:\min_i(F_vz)_i\ge-49/25\}\).

definitions.name: Exhibited four-label atomic dual
definitions.construction: Place risk mass \(1/2\) at each of \((1/\sqrt2,2)\) and \((-1/\sqrt2,2)\), coverage mass \(\lambda_4=90909437727/50000000000\) for each of labels \(02\) and \(12\) at \((0,2)\), and zero coverage mass for the other labels. Substitute these measures into the exact Lagrange-dual integral defining \(L_4\).

definitions.name: Exhibited four-label contact rule
definitions.construction: The rule \(K_{\mathrm{ct}}\) ignores its observation, reports all four labels with probability \(14/15\), and reports each singleton with probability \(1/60\).

definitions.name: Compatible observed-law polytope
definitions.construction:
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 =\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal J):\mathcal F(q)\ne\varnothing\}.
\]

definitions.name: Common-ray Følner recession library
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathscr R\) be the finite set of primitive rational ray generators in a common rational simplicial refinement of \(\operatorname{recFan}(\mathfrak G)\). For a Markov kernel \(q\), a ray \(\varrho\in\mathscr R\), and rational \(L>0\), define the one-sided Følner operator
\[
 (\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}q)(w,A)
 =\frac1L\int_0^Lq(w+t\varrho,A)\,dt,
 \qquad A\in\mathcal A.
\]
For a simplicial cone \(\sigma\), let
\[
 \mathsf A_{\sigma,L}=\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)}
 \mathsf A_{\varrho,L},
 \qquad q_{\sigma,L}=\mathsf A_{\sigma,L}q_s,
 \qquad q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}.
\]
The product uses the same operator for a ray in every incident cone. For a face inclusion \(\tau\preceq\sigma\), the transition is the product over \(\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)\). Compact normal quotients are triangulated by one global rational simplicial complex, and every vertex on a common face is represented by one shared action-probability variable.

definitions.name: Diagonal lawful comparison-window schedule
definitions.construction:
For \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\le k\}\), let \(d_n(B_k)\) be the centered local-expansion error, let \(\delta_n(B_k)=\max_j\sup_{u\in B_k}|e_{n,j}(u)|\), let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}=C_{2/\kappa}|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|/\sqrt n\), and let \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(B_k)\) be the explicit Gaussian Hellinger bound used in \(\text{thm:fixed-stratum-transfer}\). Choose rational \(\tau_k\downarrow0\) with \(\mathfrak b_0(2\tau_k)\le1/(2k)\), and let \(\mathscr E_n(k)\) be the sum of these terms, the finite-arrangement error from \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\), and \(\|c_n\|_\infty\). Define
\[
 R_n^{\diamond}=\max\left(\{0\}\cup\left\{1\le k\le n:
 B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n,\ \min_{u\in B_k,j}p_{n,j}(u)\ge\kappa/2,
 \ \mathscr E_n(\ell)\le1/\ell\ \text{for every }1\le\ell\le k\right\}\right).
\]
This is the diagonal comparison window determined by the displayed expansion, covariance, Carter, offset, and finite-arrangement moduli.
inputs: the compact expansion and covariance moduli

definitions.name: Expanding-window honest minimax profile
definitions.construction:
With \(R_n^{\diamond}\) from \(\text{def:comparison-window-schedule}\), define
\[
 \mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}^{\diamond}
 =\left\{K_n:\inf_{v\in V}\inf_{u\in D_{n,v}\cap B_{R_n^{\diamond}}}
 \Pr_{p_n(u)}\{v\in K_n(N_n)\}\ge1-\eta_0\right\},
\]
\[
 H_{n,r_0}^{\diamond}=H_{n,r_0}\cap B_{R_n^{\diamond}},
 \qquad
 M_n^{\diamond}=\inf_{K_n\in\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}^{\diamond}}
 \sup_{u\in H_{n,r_0}^{\diamond}}
 E_{p_n(u)}[\ell_0\{K_n(N_n)\}].
\]
Coverage and risk are therefore restricted to one expanding lawful window; no assertion about the exterior of that window is built into the definition.

statements.statement: For \(K_s(w)=E[K(w+s\Sigma^{1/2}\xi)]\), \(\xi\sim N_d(0,I_d)\), and every action functional \(f\in[0,R_f]\), \[\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^d}|E_hf\{K_s(W)\}-E_hf\{K(W)\}|\le R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\},\] and \(\|K_s(w)-K_s(w')\|_1\le\sqrt{2/\pi}\|w-w'\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}/s\).
statements.justification: The uniform kernel-independent bound converts arbitrary measurable honest rules into quantitatively gridable rules.
statements.gap: Jones and Peet smooth a discontinuous terminal cost inside a fixed Gaussian integral; they do not smooth an arbitrary randomized rule uniformly over all shifted means.
statements.consumer: The finite-rule enumeration uses this modulus to choose observation meshes without regularity assumptions on a near-minimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(K_A(w)=K(A\mid w)\) and \(F_K^f(w)=\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}f(A)K_A(w)\). Then \(0\le F_K^f\le R_f\), and Fubini's theorem gives
\[
 E_hF_{K_s}^f(W)
 =\int F_K^f(x)\,dN_d\{h,(1+s^2)\Sigma\}(x).
\]
The unsmoothed expectation is the same integral with \(N_d(h,\Sigma)\). For \(P_s=N_d\{h,(1+s^2)\Sigma\}\) and \(P_0=N_d(h,\Sigma)\), direct substitution in the Gaussian likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_s\Vert P_0)
 =\frac d2\{s^2-\log(1+s^2)\}.
\]
For \(x\ge0\), \(x-\log(1+x)\le x^2/2\), because the derivative of \(x^2/2-x+\log(1+x)\) is \(x^2/(1+x)\). Hence
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_s\Vert P_0)\le \frac{ds^4}{4}.
\]
Let \(A\) be a likelihood-ratio upper level set attaining total variation and put \(v=P_s(A)-P_0(A)\ge0\). The log-sum inequality reduces relative entropy to the binary experiment on \(\{A,A^c\}\). For binary probabilities \(q+v\) and \(q\), two differentiations in \(v\), followed by minimization over \(0\le q\le1-v\), give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\operatorname{Bern}(q+v)\Vert\operatorname{Bern}(q)\}\ge2v^2.
\]
Thus the elementary Pinsker bound yields
\[
 \|P_s-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_s\Vert P_0)/2}
 \le s^2\sqrt{d/8}.
\]
The total-variation distance is also at most one. Since the difference of the expectations of a function with range in \([0,R_f]\) is at most \(R_f\|P_s-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), this proves
\[
 \sup_h\left|E_hf\{K_s(W)\}-E_hf\{K(W)\}\right|
 \le R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\}.
\]
For the pointwise modulus, \(K_s(w)\) is obtained by applying the Markov kernel \(K\) to \(N_d(w,s^2\Sigma)\). Contraction of total variation under a Markov kernel therefore gives
\[
 \|K_s(w)-K_s(w')\|_1
 \le 2\|N_d(w,s^2\Sigma)-N_d(w',s^2\Sigma)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
If \(a=\|w-w'\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}/s\), the likelihood-ratio halfspace calculation for two equal-covariance Gaussian laws gives their total-variation distance as \(2\Phi(a/2)-1\). Since \(\Phi(x)-1/2\le x/\sqrt{2\pi}\) for \(x\ge0\),
\[
 \|K_s(w)-K_s(w')\|_1
 \le \sqrt{\frac2\pi}\,\frac{\|w-w'\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}}{s}.
\]
All divisions use \(s>0\), and the Mahalanobis norm is defined because \(\Sigma\succ0\).

statements.statement: For a recession stratum \(\sigma\), a \(\Sigma\)-orthogonal tangential basis \(B_{\sigma}\), and \(Q_T(w)=(2T)^{-k}\int_{[-T,T]^k}K_s(w+t u+B_{\sigma}z)\,dz\), \[\|Q_T(w+B_{\sigma}a)-Q_T(w)\|_1\le\min\{2,\|a\|_1/T\},\] and integrating out the independent residual tangential Gaussian coordinate changes any \([0,R_f]\)-valued expectation by at most \(R_fk/(T\sqrt{2\pi})\) on every declared bounded normal chart.
statements.justification: This is the quantitative local replacement step that neutralizes oscillatory behavior at infinity without assuming a recession limit.
statements.gap: Burgos Gil and Sombra control incidence geometry qualitatively, while no located statistical result supplies this rule-level tangential averaging bound.
statements.consumer: Each recession chart receives a finite normal-dimensional approximation with an explicit error allocation.
statements.proof_tex:
Choose the tangential coordinates so that the columns of \(B_\sigma\) are orthonormal after whitening by \(\Sigma^{-1/2}\), and let \(U_T\) be uniform on \([-T,T]^k\), where \(T>0\). The displayed average is
\[
 Q_T(w)=E\{K_s(w+t u+B_\sigma U_T)\}.
\]
For \(a\in\mathbb R^k\), contraction under the kernel \(z\mapsto K_s(w+t u+B_\sigma z)\) implies
\[
 \|Q_T(w+B_\sigma a)-Q_T(w)\|_1
 \le \|\mathcal L(U_T+a)-\mathcal L(U_T)\|_1.
\]
In one coordinate the last \(L^1\)-distance is \(\min\{2,|a_i|/T\}\). Coupling the product uniforms coordinate by coordinate, or equivalently bounding the symmetric difference of the two boxes, gives
\[
 \|\mathcal L(U_T+a)-\mathcal L(U_T)\|_1
 \le \min\left\{2,\frac{\|a\|_1}{T}\right\}.
\]
This proves the first assertion without any limiting behavior of \(K\).

For the second assertion, the \(\Sigma\)-orthogonal quotient decomposition makes the residual tangential observation \(B_\sigma Z\), with \(Z\sim N_k(0,I_k)\), independent of the normal coordinate and parameter-free. If \(p,p'\) are two action distributions and \(0\le f\le R_f\), the zero-sum identity for \(p-p'\) gives
\[
 \left|\sum_A f(A)\{p_A-p'_A\}\right|
 \le \frac{R_f}{2}\|p-p'\|_1.
\]
Conditioning on the normal coordinate and using the first bound with \(a=Z\),
\[
 \left|E f\{Q_T(W_N+B_\sigma Z)\}-E f\{Q_T(W_N)\}\right|
 \le \frac{R_f}{2T}E\|Z\|_1
 =\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\]
because \(E|Z_i|=\sqrt{2/\pi}\). The bounded-normal-chart condition is used only to ensure that the declared quotient chart and the associated coverage or separated-risk mean set are valid throughout this averaging operation.

statements.statement: For the glued rule \(\widetilde K(w)=\sum_i\lambda_i(w)q_i(w)\), every mean cell \(C\), anchor \(a(C)\), specified incidence paths, and \([0,R_f]\)-valued action functional \(f\), \[|E_hF_{\widetilde K}^{f}(W)-E_hF_{a(C)}^{f}(W)|\le\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^{f}+R_f\omega(h)/2\] uniformly on the declared coverage or separated-risk mean domain, including means centered on seams.
statements.justification: The inequality prevents uncharged off-neighborhood and weight-variation errors from invalidating a finite gluing certificate.
statements.gap: The polyhedral compactification literature proves that charts meet correctly but has no Gaussian-weighted rule-discrepancy inequality.
statements.consumer: An independent verifier can replay every seam and path charge in the primal certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(F_i^f(w)=\sum_A f(A)q_{i,A}(w)\) and \(F_{\widetilde K}^f(w)=\sum_i\lambda_i(w)F_i^f(w)\). Orient every path from the anchor \(a(C)\) to \(i\). Telescoping along that path gives
\[
 F_i^f(w)-F_{a(C)}^f(w)
 =\sum_{e\in\pi_C(i)}\{F_{e^+}^f(w)-F_{e^-}^f(w)\}.
\]
Multiplication by \(\lambda_i(w)\ge0\), summation over \(i\), and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 |F_{\widetilde K}^f(w)-F_{a(C)}^f(w)|
 \le \sum_e g_{C,e}(w)|F_{e^+}^f(w)-F_{e^-}^f(w)|,
 \qquad
 g_{C,e}(w)=\sum_{i:e\in\pi_C(i)}\lambda_i(w).
\]
Both endpoint functionals lie in \([0,R_f]\). Splitting the integral for edge \(e\) over \(P_{C,e}\) and \(P_{C,e}^c\) consequently yields, for every \(h\in M_{C,f}\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_h\!\left[g_{C,e}(W)|F_{e^+}^f(W)-F_{e^-}^f(W)|\right]
 &\le \int_{P_{C,e}}g_{C,e}|F_{e^+}^f-F_{e^-}^f|\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw\\
 &\quad+R_f\int_{P_{C,e}^c}g_{C,e}\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw\\
 &\le \Gamma_{C,e}^f.
 \end{split}
\]
Thus the left side in the claim is at most \(\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f\). The supremum is over the entire declared mean set and therefore includes seam-centered means.

For completeness, let \(d_i=\lambda_i(W)-\lambda_i(h)\). Since \(\sum_i d_i=0\) and \(0\le F_i^f\le R_f\),
\[
 \left|\sum_i d_iF_i^f(W)\right|
 \le \frac{R_f}{2}\sum_i|d_i|.
\]
Taking \(E_h\) proves the separate weight-variation estimate \(R_f\omega(h)/2\). Adding this nonnegative certified remainder to the sharper path bound proves the stated inequality.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\), the value \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) is attained by a globally honest randomized rule and equals the supremum of the Lagrange dual over finite nonnegative atomic coverage measures on the regions \(D_v\) and finite atomic probability measures on \(H_r\). Every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate. An increasing enumeration of finite atomic certificates with rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points converges upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), without a bounded-support premise.
statements.justification: Attainment and dense atomic duality identify the exact object that the outward primal and dual programs must enclose.
statements.gap: Goldenshluger, Juditsky, and Nemirovski establish compact-convex pairwise detector saddles, and Schafer and Stark approximate compact-parameter minimax expected size; neither treats globally honest finite-label rules over an unbounded fan.
statements.consumer: CertGluePFL obtains valid lower endpoints without assuming that least-favorable mass is spatially tight.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: local weak compactness followed by finite-dimensional convex
separation.}
Let \(\mu\) be Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R^d\), and write a Markov
kernel as
\[
 p=(p_A)_{A\in\mathcal A},\qquad
 p_A\geq0,\qquad \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}p_A=1
 \quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\tag{1}
\]
Denote the set in (1) by \(\mathscr K\).  This representation is exact because
\(\mathcal A=2^V\) is finite.  Put \(B_j=[-j,j]^d\), and give
\(\mathscr K\) the coordinatewise weak topology of \(L^2(B_j)\), for every
\(A\in\mathcal A\) and \(j\geq1\).

We first prove compactness rather than assume it.  For every \(p\in\mathscr K\),
\[
 \|p_A\|_{L^2(B_j)}\leq\mu(B_j)^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
Choose a countable orthonormal basis of each \(L^2(B_j)\).  From any sequence
in \(\mathscr K\), diagonal extraction makes all its Fourier coefficients,
over the countable triples consisting of an action, a box, and a basis
element, converge.  The bounds (2) and Bessel's inequality identify the
coefficient limits with weak \(L^2(B_j)\) limits.  Limits on nested boxes
agree, because a test function on \(B_j\), extended by zero, is a test
function on \(B_{j+1}\).  They therefore define measurable functions
\(p_A\) on \(\mathbb R^d\).

The constraints in (1) are weakly closed.  Indeed, for nonnegative
\(q\in L^2(B_j)\), weak convergence gives
\(\int_{B_j}p_Aq\,d\mu\geq0\).  Taking \(q=(p_A)_-\) proves
\(p_A\geq0\); applying the same argument to \(1-p_A\) proves \(p_A\leq1\).
Testing \(\sum_Ap_A-1\) against its positive and negative parts proves
\(\sum_Ap_A=1\).  The bounded Fourier coefficients metrize this
coordinatewise local weak topology.  The diagonal argument thus proves
sequential compactness in a metric space, and hence compactness of
\(\mathscr K\).  Convexity is immediate from (1).

For \(v\in V\), \(h\in D_v\), and \(g\in H_r\), define
\[
 c_{v,h}(p)=
 \int_{\mathbb R^d}\phi_\Sigma(w-h)
       \sum_{A\ni v}p_A(w)\,dw,
 \qquad
 r_g(p)=
 \int_{\mathbb R^d}\phi_\Sigma(w-g)
       \sum_A\ell(A)p_A(w)\,dw.
\tag{3}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:rational\mbox{-}positive\mbox{-}covariance}\)
implies that every translated Gaussian density is in \(L^2(B_j)\).  Hence
local weak convergence gives convergence of (3) over \(B_j\).  Outside
\(B_j\), the two errors are bounded, respectively, by the translated
Gaussian tail and by \(D\) times that tail, uniformly over \(p\in\mathscr K\).
First sending the kernel index to infinity and then \(j\) to infinity proves
that every functional in (3) is continuous.

By the definition of \(\mathcal C_\eta\), its image in \(\mathscr K\) is
\[
 \mathscr K_\eta=
 \bigcap_{v\in V}\ \bigcap_{h\in D_v}
 \{p\in\mathscr K:c_{v,h}(p)\geq1-\eta\}.
\tag{4}
\]
It is compact by continuity of (3), and it is nonempty because the rule that
always reports \(V\) lies in it.  By
\(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}profile}\), the objective is
\(p\mapsto\sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p)\).  It is lower semicontinuous as a
supremum of continuous functions.  It therefore attains its minimum on
\(\mathscr K_\eta\).  All \(N_d(h,\Sigma)\) are equivalent to \(\mu\) because
\(\Sigma\succ0\); changing the finitely many coordinates on one common null
set makes the minimizer a pointwise Markov kernel without changing any
coverage or risk.  This proves primal attainment.

We next prove weak duality and exact atomic exhaustion.  Let
\[
 \alpha_v=\sum_{j=1}^{J_v}a_{vj}\delta_{h_{vj}},
 \quad a_{vj}\geq0,\quad h_{vj}\in D_v,
 \qquad
 \beta=\sum_{i=1}^{I}b_i\delta_{g_i},
 \quad b_i\geq0,\quad\sum_i b_i=1,\quad g_i\in H_r,
\tag{5}
\]
and put
\[
 a_v(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,\alpha_v(dh),
 \qquad
 b(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\,\beta(dg).
\tag{6}
\]
The Lagrangian for the risk epigraph and the coverage inequalities is
\[
 (1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 \int_{\mathbb R^d}\sum_{A\subseteq V}p_A(w)
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}\,dw .
\tag{7}
\]
At each \(w\), (1) is a finite simplex.  Selecting the first minimizing
action in a fixed enumeration is measurable.  Thus the infimum of (7) over
\(\mathscr K\) equals
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)=
 (1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 \int_{\mathbb R^d}\min_{A\subseteq V}
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}\,dw .
\tag{8}
\]
For \(p\in\mathscr K_\eta\), Tonelli's theorem applies to the nonnegative
mixtures in (6), and (3)--(8) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 &\leq
 \sum_i b_i r_{g_i}(p)
 +\sum_{v,j}a_{vj}\{(1-\eta)-c_{v,h_{vj}}(p)\}\\
 &\leq \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Therefore every displayed finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate.

For the converse, fix \(t<M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The open sets
\[
 \{p:r_g(p)>t\}\quad(g\in H_r),\qquad
 \{p:c_{v,h}(p)<1-\eta\}\quad(v\in V,\ h\in D_v)
\tag{10}
\]
cover \(\mathscr K\).  Indeed, an honest kernel has supremum risk at least
\(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)>t\), whereas a nonhonest kernel violates one
inequality in (4).  Compactness supplies a finite subcover with risk points
\(g_1,\ldots,g_I\) and coverage pairs
\((v_j,h_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,J\).  The set
\[
 Y=\left\{
 \bigl((r_{g_i}(p)-t)_{i\leq I},
 ((1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p))_{j\leq J}\bigr):
 p\in\mathscr K
 \right\}
\tag{11}
\]
is compact and convex, and the finite-subcover property says that it is
disjoint from the closed negative orthant \(O\).

For completeness, we derive the required separator.  Choose
\(y_*\in Y\) minimizing the squared distance to \(O\), let \(z_*\) be its
coordinatewise projection on \(O\), and set \(n=y_*-z_*\).  Then
\(n\geq0\), \(n'z_*=0\), and \(n'y_*=\|n\|_2^2>0\).  For \(y\in Y\),
apply minimality to \(y_*+s(y-y_*)\in Y\), divide the resulting squared
distance inequality by \(s>0\), and let \(s\downarrow0\).  This gives
\(n'y\geq n'y_*\).  Consequently there are
\(\gamma_i,\zeta_j\geq0\), not all zero, and \(q>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_i\gamma_i\{r_{g_i}(p)-t\}
 +\sum_j\zeta_j\{(1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p)\}
 \geq q
 \quad\text{for all }p\in\mathscr K.
\tag{12}
\]
For the kernel that always reports \(V\), every coverage deficit in (12)
equals \(-\eta\).  Hence \(G=\sum_i\gamma_i>0\), since otherwise (12)
would have a nonpositive left side.  Set \(b_i=\gamma_i/G\), and place
coverage mass \(\zeta_j/G\) at \((v_j,h_j)\).  Divide (12) by \(G\), take
the infimum over \(\mathscr K\), and use (8) to obtain
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)\geq t+\frac qG>t.
\tag{13}
\]
Together with (9), and then \(t\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), this
proves
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 =\sup_{\alpha,\beta\ {\rm finite\ atomic}}\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta).
\tag{14}
\]
This argument never restricts the spatial support of either measure.

It remains to verify the effective support and value assertions.  Every
\(D_v\) is a finite union of rational polyhedra.  For a rational polyhedron
\(\{x:Ax\leq b\}\), the squared \(\Sigma^{-1}\)-distance is obtained by
partitioning according to the finitely many active sets of its strictly
convex quadratic projection problem.  On each active-set piece, primal
feasibility, stationarity, complementary slackness, and a distance
comparison with \(r^2\) are finite polynomial equalities and inequalities
in the displayed variables.  Taking the finite disjunction over components,
labels, and active sets gives a finite exact semialgebraic description of
\(H_r\).  Recursive sign decomposition of these finitely many polynomials
has two relevant constructive properties: on a rational box it terminates,
and it either certifies emptiness or isolates a sample whose coordinates
are represented by rational isolating intervals and minimal polynomials.
Enumerating rational boxes and retaining the nonempty cells therefore
produces dense, effectively enumerable, rationally encoded real-algebraic
samples in every \(D_v\) and in \(H_r\), including lower-dimensional cells.
The nonemptiness of \(H_r\) used here is
\(\mathrm{ass:separated\mbox{-}domain\mbox{-}nonempty}\).

If \(x_n\to x\), then
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R^d}
 |\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n)-\phi_\Sigma(w-x)|\,dw
 =
 2-2\int_{\mathbb R^d}
 \min\{\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n),\phi_\Sigma(w-x)\}\,dw
 \longrightarrow0
\tag{15}
\]
by pointwise convergence and dominated convergence.  Thus finitely many
support points can be perturbed inside their respective sets, and their
weights can be perturbed to nonnegative rationals while keeping
\(\sum_i b_i=1\), so that all mixtures in (6) converge in \(L^1\).  Since
\[
 \left|\min_A x_A-\min_A y_A\right|
 \leq\max_A|x_A-y_A|,
\tag{16}
\]
the corresponding values (8) converge.  Rational weights and rationally
encoded real-algebraic support points are therefore dense among all finite
atomic certificates.

Finally, the value of each encoded certificate is a computable real.  On a
rational box, interval Taylor bounds for the finitely many Gaussian
mixtures and their derivatives give convergent rational lower and upper
Riemann bounds for the finite minimum in (8).  Off the box, the absolute
integrand is bounded by
\(D b(w)+\sum_v a_v(w)\), whose finitely many Gaussian tails have effective
outward rational bounds.  Enumerate all encoded atomic certificates and
dovetail these shrinking two-sided enclosures.  Start from any enumerated
certificate and replace the current one only when another certificate's
certified lower endpoint exceeds the current certificate's certified upper
endpoint.  The exact selected values are nondecreasing.  If their limit
were below the supremum in (14), an already enumerated certificate with a
strictly larger value would eventually have that strict inequality
certified, a contradiction.  Hence the selected finite atomic certificates
converge upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), proving every assertion of
the theorem.

statements.statement:
Assume, as an additional displayed premise, either the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\) or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package providing the same computable finite-library modulus and verifiable ledgers.  Then, for every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\operatorname{CertGluePFL}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\) terminates and returns a replayable globally honest primal rule, a finite rational atomic dual certificate, and outward rational endpoints
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
It also returns explicit total recursive bounds \(N_{\mathrm{glue}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{cut}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{Gauss}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{LP}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), and \(\operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), recorded in \(\mathsf C\).  The theorem is conditional and does not assert an affirmative answer to \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\).
statements.justification: A convergence theorem without a finite stopping recurrence would not support certified statistical practice.
statements.gap: Jones and Peet give an a priori integration error, Jungen, Djelassi, and Mitsos give conditional convergence for finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs, and Cousins and Vempala give randomized Gaussian-volume approximation; none certifies this function-valued minimax game with exact honesty and a matched atomic dual.
statements.consumer: For the Job Corps assertion list, the output archives the exact observed-cell-to-\(\mathfrak G_0\) encoding, the simultaneous honest label rule, the primal and atomic-dual objects, and every outward integration and repair charge; this replayable certificate is required because a floating-point optimizer cannot establish global honesty on tied capacity, sign, or cross-quantile faces.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: effective dovetailing of sound primal and dual semidecisions.}

The extra premise in the theorem is used conditionally; it is not derived from the standing assumptions.  Write \(\mathsf{ECD}(\mathfrak G)\) for the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or for a separately proved package having exactly the same consequences.  Thus there are a computable sequence \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\in\mathbb Q_+\) with \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\downarrow0\), enumerable finite records \(Q_j(K)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\), and verifiable outward ledgers such that, for every \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 c\{Q_j(K)\}&\ge 1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
 r\{Q_j(K)\}&\le R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}\{Q_j(K)\}&\le \Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j).
 \end{split}
 \tag{1}
\]
Here
\[
 c(Q)=\inf_{v\in V}\inf_{h\in D_v}P_h\{v\in Q(W)\},
 \qquad
 r(Q)=\sup_{h\in H_r}E_h\ell\{Q(W)\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The five simultaneous geometric obligations in that affirmative conclusion ensure that (1) is a single compatible record: the chart, collar, path, translated-tail, weight-variation, integration, covariance, rounding, and repair charges all occur in the ledger of \(\text{def:weighted-error-ledger}\).  This is the only use of \(\mathsf{ECD}(\mathfrak G)\).

At stage \(s\), the search in \(\text{def:certglue-handle}\) enumerates all indices \(j\le s\), all codes of length at most \(s\) for members of \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\), all rational incidence forests and semantic projections, all rational action probabilities, and the first \(s\) choices of integration and rounding precision.  Each candidate is accepted only after exact rational or real-algebraic geometry checks and outward Gaussian integration give rational numbers
\[
 c^-_{Q,s}\le c(Q),
 \qquad
 r(Q)\le r^+_{Q,s}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The protected-neighborhood integrals, their complements, and every path load are precisely those declared in \(\text{def:weighted-error-ledger}\).  Consequently (3) is sound even on equality faces and unbounded charts; no floating-point sign is used.

Replace \(c^-_{Q,s}\) by its intersection with \([0,1]\), and define
\[
 \rho_{Q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{Q,s}\},
 \qquad
 q_{Q,s}=\frac{\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Because \(0<\eta<1/2\) and \(0\le c^-_{Q,s}\le1\),
\[
 0\le\rho_{Q,s}\le1-\eta<1,
 \qquad \eta+\rho_{Q,s}>0,
 \tag{5}
\]
so the division in (4) is valid.  Moreover, (3)--(4) give \(c(Q)\ge1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s}\).  Apply \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) and let \(Q^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho_{Q,s}}(Q)\).  Then \(Q^+\in\mathcal C_\eta\) and
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 \le R_r(Q^+)
 \le r^+_{Q,s}+\frac{D\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.
 \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, the coverage identity underlying the repair is
\[
 \left(1-q_{Q,s}\right)(1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s})+q_{Q,s}=1-\eta,
 \tag{7}
\]
and \(0\le\ell\le D\) gives the risk increment in (6).  Outward rational arithmetic therefore returns a rational \(U_{Q,s}\) no smaller than the last member of (6).

In parallel, enumerate the finite nonnegative atomic dual records supplied by \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\).  Their rational weights and rational real-algebraic support encodings permit exact feasibility checks against the finite rational-polyhedral unions \(D_v\), the singleton-label condition, and the quadratic distance inequalities defining \(H_r\).  Refining the outward Gaussian enclosures gives a rational lower value \(l^-_{\nu,s}\) for every processed feasible dual record \(\nu\).  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), each such value is a valid lower certificate.  Set
\[
 L_s=\max_{\nu\ \mathrm{processed\ by}\ s}l^-_{\nu,s},
 \qquad
 U_s=\min_{Q\ \mathrm{accepted\ by}\ s}U_{Q,s},
 \tag{8}
\]
with an endpoint left undefined until its finite indexing set is nonempty.  Weak duality and (6) imply
\[
 L_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\le U_s
 \tag{9}
\]
whenever both endpoints are defined.

Every fixed stage terminates.  There are only finitely many codes at that stage.  Rational-polyhedral incidence, linear programming, and real-algebraic sign tests terminate.  On a rational box the Gaussian density and each accepted piecewise-rational integrand have computable uniform enclosures away from their finitely described boundaries, while boundary collars have explicitly charged Gaussian mass.  Recursive subdivision therefore drives the box error to zero.  Positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\), from \(\text{ass:rational-positive-covariance}\), supplies an explicit Gaussian tail bound tending to zero as the box expands.  Hence each requested positive enclosure width is reached after finitely many subdivisions.

It remains to prove that the rational stopping test is eventually satisfied.  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is \(K^*\in\mathcal C_\eta\) with
\[
 R_r(K^*)=M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
 \tag{10}
\]
Apply (1) to \(K^*\).  Given a rational \(\zeta>0\), sufficiently fine evaluation of the resulting finite record yields
\[
 c^-_{Q_j(K^*),s}\ge c\{Q_j(K^*)\}-\zeta,
 \qquad
 r^+_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le r\{Q_j(K^*)\}+\zeta.
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (1), (4), and (11) imply
\[
 \rho_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta.
 \tag{12}
\]
Using (1), (6), and (10)--(12), and charging at most one further \(\zeta\) for final outward rounding, gives
\[
 U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 +D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+2\zeta
 +\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\}}
 {\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(\eta>0\).  First let \(j\to\infty\), and then let \(\zeta\downarrow0\).  The right side of (13) tends to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The final assertion of \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\) supplies an enumerated sequence of finite atomic lower certificates converging upward to the same value.  Thus
\[
 L_s\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r),
 \qquad
 \limsup_{s\to\infty}U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
 \tag{14}
\]
Together with (9), this proves that some finite stage has \(U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\).

Finally, expose the promised total recurrences.  For \(i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}\), let \(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the number of operations of type \(i\) performed at stage \(s\), and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest bit length appearing there.  Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_i(0)&=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),&
 C_i(s+1)&=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),\\
 B(0)&=b(\mathfrak G,0),&
 B(s+1)&=\max\{B(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{15}
\]
Let
\[
 s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
 =\min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\}.
 \tag{16}
\]
The predicate in (16) is a rational decidable predicate, and (14) proves that its sequential search halts.  Hence \(s_*\) is total recursive under the displayed conditional premise.  Set
\[
 N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
 \quad i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=B\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Archive at stage \(s_*\) the repaired primal attaining the finite minimum in (8), the atomic dual attaining its finite maximum, every outward enclosure, and the recurrences (15)--(17).  Equations (9), (16), and (17) give the asserted endpoints, exact global honesty, termination, and five-part receipt.  All of these conclusions remain conditional on \(\mathsf{ECD}(\mathfrak G)\).

Let \(p_n(0)=p_0\), put \(m=|\mathcal J|\), and fix a compact \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) that is eventually contained in \(\mathcal U_n\) and lies in one completed positive-support stratum.  Fix a Gaussian rule for \(\mathfrak G_0\) whose finite representation has Gaussian-null boundaries.  Define
\[
d_n(C)=\sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2,
\qquad
\delta_n(C)=\max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|,
\]
with the maximum equal to zero when \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}=\varnothing\), and set
\[
A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}},
\qquad x_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C).
\]
There is a parameter-independent Carter transfer producing \(K_n\) for which every semantic coverage probability and every normalized diameter-risk expectation on \(C\) differs from its Gaussian counterpart by at most
\[
\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{lin}}(C)
=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}
+(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).
\]
Here \(H_C\) is obtained by finite rational active-set enumeration, and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\) is the explicit Hellinger bound between the score-normal law and \(N_d(u,\Sigma_0)\).  Consequently \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{lin}}(C)\to0\).  Carter's theorem is used only for the multinomial--matched-normal comparison; semantic stability and covariance replacement are the two separately displayed terms.  No overall \(O(n^{-1/2})\) rate is asserted without corresponding rates for \(x_n(C)\) and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\).
statements.justification: The revised theorem gives the first complete Carter-backed compact comparison receipt.
statements.gap: Its new proof separates Carter's total-variation term from score covariance and semantic arrangement stability.
statements.consumer: Job Corps cell counts inherit compact coverage and diameter-risk guarantees.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: parameter-independent Le Cam transfer, affine scoring, Gaussian Hellinger comparison, and finite-arrangement stability.}

Put \(D_0=\operatorname{diag}(p_0)\), \(I_0=B'D_0^{-1}B\), and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\).  The inverse exists.  Indeed, \(\min_j(p_0)_j\ge\kappa>0\) by \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), and \(B\) has column rank \(d\), so for every \(z\ne0\),
\[
 z'I_0z=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\frac{\{(Bz)_j\}^2}{(p_0)_j}>0.
 \tag{18}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\).

By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), the bounded-ratio condition holds uniformly on \(C\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and Carter's parameter-independent kernel sends the multinomial count experiment to its matched normal count experiment with total-variation error at most
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}
 =C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}.
 \tag{19}
\]
For a matched normal count vector \(Y_n\), apply the parameter-independent affine score
\[
 S_n(Y_n)=\Sigma_0B'D_0^{-1}\frac{Y_n-np_0}{\sqrt n}.
 \tag{20}
\]
At local parameter \(u\), this score is normal with mean and covariance
\[
 \mu_n(u)=\Sigma_0B'D_0^{-1}\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_0\},
 \tag{21}
\]
\[
 V_n(u)=\Sigma_0B'D_0^{-1}
 [\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(u)\}-p_n(u)p_n(u)']
 D_0^{-1}B\Sigma_0.
 \tag{22}
\]
Since \(\Sigma_0B'D_0^{-1}B=I_d\),
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\|\mu_n(u)-u\|_2
 \le \|\Sigma_0B'D_0^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}d_n(C).
 \tag{23}
\]
The local expansion gives \(d_n(C)\to0\), while \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\), continuity of \(p\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp'\), and compactness give
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\|V_n(u)-\Sigma_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{24}
\]

For positive definite \(V\), define the explicit squared Hellinger distance
\[
 \mathsf H^2(\mu,V;u,\Sigma_0)
 =2-2\frac{|V|^{1/4}|\Sigma_0|^{1/4}}
 {|(V+\Sigma_0)/2|^{1/2}}
 \exp\!\left[-\frac18(\mu-u)'
 \{(V+\Sigma_0)/2\}^{-1}(\mu-u)\right].
 \tag{25}
\]
Completing the square in the product of the two Gaussian densities gives (25).  If \(p\) and \(q\) are any two densities, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \frac12\int|p-q|
 =\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)
 \le\left\{\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
Thus total variation is at most the Hellinger distance in the normalization (25), and we obtain the outward-computable bound
\[
 \operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 =\sup_{u\in C}\min\{1,
 \mathsf H(\mu_n(u),V_n(u);u,\Sigma_0)\}.
 \tag{26}
\]
Equations (23)--(24), eventual uniform positive definiteness, and continuity of (25) on the compact parameter set imply
\[
 \operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{27}
\]

Let \(x_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)\).  Apply \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) to the fixed finite completed arrangement and enlarge its finite rational active-set constant, if necessary, to absorb the fixed norm conversions and the equal-covariance Gaussian translation bound.  Then all chart and semantic correspondences on \(C\), including the directed separation-distance comparison for rival semantic unions, contribute at most
\[
 H_Cx_n(C).
 \tag{28}
\]
Equality faces cause no loss because the completed convention assigns every incident label to the face.  The assumed Gaussian-null boundaries of the finite representation allow boundary equalities to be changed without changing any probability.

It remains to charge observations for which an active affine sign can change.  For \(j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\), \(a_j\ne0\); (18) therefore gives \(a_j'\Sigma_0a_j>0\).  If \(W_0\sim N_d(h,\Sigma_0)\), the density of \(a_j'W_0\) is bounded, uniformly in \(h\), by \(\{2\pi a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{-1/2}\).  Hence, for every \(s\ge0\),
\[
 \Pr_h\{|a_j'W_0|\le s\}
 \le\min\left\{1,
 \frac{2s}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}
 \right\}.
 \tag{29}
\]
The union bound gives
\[
 \mathfrak b_0(s)\le A_0s,
 \qquad
 A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
 \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}.
 \tag{30}
\]
When the active list is empty, both sides of (30) are zero.  Split the comparison according to the union of the slabs in (29), using width \(s=x_n(C)\).  Off those slabs, the completed active signs agree and (28) applies; on the slabs, both a coverage indicator and the normalized loss lie in \([0,1]\), so their discrepancy is bounded by the slab probability.  Therefore the total geometry charge is at most
\[
 (H_C+A_0)x_n(C).
 \tag{31}
\]

Apply \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\) to Carter's kernel and to the Gaussian comparison (26), first with \(A\mapsto\mathbf1\{v\in A\}\) and then with \(A\mapsto\ell_0(A)\).  Both functions take values in \([0,1]\).  Adding (19), (26), and (31) proves that every stated compact semantic-coverage probability and normalized diameter-risk expectation differs from its Gaussian counterpart by at most
\[
 \mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{lin}}(C)
 =C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}
 +(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).
 \tag{32}
\]
Finally, \(d_n(C)\to0\) by \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), and \(\delta_n(C)\to0\) by \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\).  Together with (27), this gives \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{lin}}(C)\to0\).  Equation (32) keeps the semantic and covariance terms separate and therefore makes no unsupported overall \(O(n^{-1/2})\) assertion.

Suppose \(p_n(0)\to p_0\), \(p_n(u)-p_0\in\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\), \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\), and \(\delta_n(C)=\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) on every rational compact polytope \(C\).  Choose rational \(\xi_n\downarrow0\) and \(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\cap\mathbb Q^{|\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}|}\) with \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\le\xi_n\).  Then \(c_n\) and \(\widehat c_n\) lie eventually in a fixed compact \(C_c\subset\mathcal K_0\), each rational offset experiment \(\mathfrak G_0(\widehat c_n)\) is a fully encoded experiment, and the unconditional comparison in \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\) applies to any supplied Gaussian rule.  In particular, with \(H_C=H(C,C_c)\), \(A_0\) as displayed there, \(\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\), and any upper bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\ge\chi_n(C)\), its comparison charge is
\[
\Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
+\{H_C+2A_0\}\overline\chi_n(C).
\]
Taking \(\overline\chi_n(C)=\chi_n(C)\) proves qualitative compact convergence and makes no effectiveness claim.  A finite replayable Gaussian rule and its gluing ledger are available only conditional on the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package.  Replayable comparison-error accounting additionally requires effective rational upper enclosures for \(d_n(C)\) and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\) to be supplied as inputs; neither those enclosures nor the Gaussian-rule construction follows from the qualitative comparison.  No global honesty or risk conclusion is asserted outside \(C\).

statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: compatible affine-offset lifting followed by the unconditional Carter--geometry comparison.}

Let \(A_\Psi\) have rows \(\alpha_j'\), \(j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\), and put \(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  Every active cut satisfies \(\psi_j(p_0)=0\), so affinity of \(\psi_j\) gives
\[
 c_n=A_\Psi\sqrt n\{p_n(0)-p_0\}.
 \tag{33}
\]
By \(\text{ass:local-family-affine-hull}\), the vector in braces belongs to \(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  The definition of \(\mathcal K_0\) therefore implies
\[
 c_n\in\mathcal K_0\qquad\text{for every }n.
 \tag{34}
\]
Choose rational \(\xi_n\downarrow0\).  The effective moving-offset encoding assumption supplies \(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\cap\mathbb Q^{|\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}|}\) with
\[
 \|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\le\xi_n.
 \tag{35}
\]
Since \(c_n\to c\), equations (35) and \(\xi_n\to0\) imply \(\widehat c_n\to c\).  Thus the two sequences lie eventually in one closed bounded subset \(C_c\) of the finite-dimensional space \(\mathcal K_0\).  It is compact, and \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) supplies the single finite constant
\[
 H_C=H(C,C_c)<\infty.
 \tag{36}
\]
This proves, rather than assumes, the compact-offset premise of \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\).

We verify that the rational offset object is a fully encoded experiment.  Because \(A_\Psi\) and a rational basis of \(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) are rational, Gaussian elimination applied to \(A_\Psi z=\widehat c_n\) returns a rational solution \(z_n\in L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  For every fixed \(u\), tangent-image compatibility gives \(Bu\in L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), hence \(z_n+Bu\in L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  By the definition of relative interior, a relative open ball about \(p_0\) in the affine hull of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  Applying this fact to the fixed direction \(z_n+Bu\) gives a number \(t_{n,u}>0\) such that
\[
 p_0+t(z_n+Bu)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 \qquad(0<t\le t_{n,u}).
 \tag{37}
\]
For an active cut,
\[
 \alpha_j'(z_n+Bu)=\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u.
 \tag{38}
\]
The compatible full-law lift in (37) has a feasible optimal completed branch with the signs in (38), and a zero sign belongs to every incident completion.  Therefore \(\bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0(\widehat c_n)=\mathbb R^d\).

If the active list is empty, \(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\) gives one global semantic label, so the separated domain is nonempty for every \(r_0\ge0\).  Otherwise choose a rational vector \(y\) outside the finite union of homogeneous hyperplanes \(a_j'y=0\).  Along \(u=ty\), every sign in (38) is eventually the fixed strict sign of \(a_j'y\); hence there is a unique completed semantic label \(v_y\) for all sufficiently large \(t\).  Every component belonging to a rival semantic label differs in at least one of these finitely many strict signs.  For that component there is a nonzero rational row \(a'\) and constants \(\gamma>0\), \(b\in\mathbb R\) such that its defining inequality implies, for every point \(g\) in the component,
\[
 t\gamma-b\le a'(ty-g)
 \le \|a\|_{\Sigma_0}\|ty-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}.
 \tag{39}
\]
The divisor is positive because \(a\ne0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\).  There are finitely many rival components, so the minimum of the lower bounds in (39) tends to infinity.  In particular, for all sufficiently large \(t\), \(ty\) has the unique label \(v_y\) and distance at least \(r_0\) from every rival semantic union.  Thus the offset separated domain is nonempty.  Rationality of the offset and the original cuts gives rational polyhedral components; \(\Sigma_0\succ0\) was proved from the rank and positivity conditions.  The rational offset object therefore belongs to \(\mathfrak E\).

For the statistical comparison, \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\) and \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) give
\[
 d_n(C)\to0,
 \qquad \delta_n(C)\to0,
 \qquad \operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\to0.
 \tag{40}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{41}
\]
Now apply \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\), whose compact-offset premise is (36).  For any supplied Gaussian rule and any supplied bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\ge\chi_n(C)\), it gives
\[
 \Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
 +\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 +\{H_C+2A_0\}\overline\chi_n(C).
 \tag{42}
\]
The mathematical choice \(\overline\chi_n(C)=\chi_n(C)\) is always valid and need not be computable.  Equations (36), (40), and (41) then imply \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).  This proves the unconditional qualitative compact comparison for every supplied Gaussian rule.

No step above constructs that Gaussian rule.  If the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or a separately proved sufficient package, is supplied, \(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) applied to the rational offset experiment produces a finite replayable Gaussian rule and its outward ledger.  Composing with Carter's forward kernel adds (42) to the ledger.  The effective moving-remainder and offset-encoding assumptions provide effective rational bounds only for \(\delta_n(C)\) and \(\xi_n\).  A replayable numerical enclosure of (42) additionally requires supplied effective rational upper enclosures for \(d_n(C)\) and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\).  This requirement is an input to the accounting, not a consequence of effective compatible density.  Since every supremum in (40)--(42) is over \(C\), the argument gives no global conclusion outside that compact set.

Assume \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\), \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\), the local-family affine-hull condition, multinomial interiority, base convergence, compact-uniform centered local expansion, effective moving-offset encoding, and \(c_n\to0\).  Let \(R_n^{\diamond}\) and \(M_n^{\diamond}\) be given by \(\text{def:comparison-window-schedule}\) and \(\text{def:windowed-multinomial-minimax}\).  These are diagonally selected expanding lawful windows; the stated compact-convergence assumptions do not assert that their selection is computable.  Then
\[
R_n^{\diamond}\to\infty,
\]
every finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate has a lawful multinomial realization inside \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\), and
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}M_n^{\diamond}
=M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
\qquad
\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\]
Conditional on the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, the Gaussian upper rules may be chosen from CertGluePFL receipts and their windowwise repairs are replayable whenever the needed finite-window comparison enclosures are supplied.  No conclusion about \(\limsup_nM_n\), no globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal, and no algorithm for selecting \(R_n^{\diamond}\) follow from the stated premises.

statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: diagonal compact exhaustion, finite-support dual transfer, and exact windowwise repair.}

Let \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\le k\}\).  Fix \(k\in\mathbb N\).  By \(\text{lem:compact-causal-domain}\), the relative-interior, affine-hull, base-convergence, and compact local-expansion premises imply
\[
 B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n
 \tag{43}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), eventually
\[
 \min_{u\in B_k}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\ge\kappa/2.
 \tag{44}
\]
For each fixed \(1\le\ell\le k\), zero-offset centering, the local expansion, \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\), and \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) make every term in \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\) tend to zero.  Since there are only finitely many such \(\ell\), (43), (44), and
\[
 \mathscr E_n(\ell)\le1/\ell,
 \qquad 1\le\ell\le k,
 \tag{45}
\]
hold simultaneously for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The definition of \(R_n^{\diamond}\) then gives \(R_n^{\diamond}\ge k\).  Since \(k\) was arbitrary,
\[
 R_n^{\diamond}\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{46}
\]
This is a diagonal existence argument; the qualitative hypotheses do not provide an algorithm deciding the eventual indices in (43)--(45).

For all sufficiently large \(n\), put \(k_n=R_n^{\diamond}\ge1\), and let \(\rho_n\) be the complete Carter, score, covariance, offset, boundary, and completed-arrangement comparison charge on \(B_{k_n}\).  In \(\text{def:comparison-window-schedule}\), the finite-arrangement term includes the directed Hausdorff comparison and the separation-restoration displacement required below.  The acceptance inequalities at \(\ell=k_n\) therefore give
\[
 0\le\rho_n\le\mathscr E_n(k_n)\le1/k_n.
 \tag{47}
\]
Thus (46) implies \(\rho_n\to0\).

We first prove the lower bound.  Let \(L<M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is a finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate \(\mu\) of value greater than \(L\).  Its finite support lies in \(B_k\) for some \(k\).  The two directed finite-arrangement comparisons realize every coverage atom \(h\in D_v^0\) by an atom \(h_n\in D_{n,v}\) with \(\|h_n-h\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\to0\).  If \(h\) is on an equality face, a separate copy is used for each dual constraint role; the completed convention retains every incident label.

Risk atoms can also be realized in the separated set.  If \(r_0>0\), the zero-offset cells are conical and distance to each rival cone is positively homogeneous.  For a risk atom \(h\in H_{r_0}\), choose \(t_n\downarrow0\) slowly enough that the extra margin of \((1+t_n)h\) dominates twice the directed Hausdorff error.  The resulting perturbed atom then lies in \(H_{n,r_0}\) and converges to \(h\).  If \(r_0=0\), the completed finite arrangement permits approximation of a singleton-label point by singleton-label chamber points; closedness of the finite rival union gives each chosen chamber point a positive atom-specific distance, after which the same directed comparison places its realization in \(H_{n,0}\).  Because the support of \(\mu\) is finite and (46) holds, all these atoms lie in \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\) eventually.  This proves the asserted lawful multinomial realization of every finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate.

Apply Carter's reverse parameter-independent kernel, followed by the score and covariance maps, to an arbitrary window-honest multinomial rule.  By \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\), the error in the finite dual objective is at most \(A_\mu\rho_n\), where \(A_\mu<\infty\) is the sum of the absolute coefficients of the fixed finite dual record.  Weak duality then yields
\[
 M_n^{\diamond}\ge L-A_\mu\rho_n.
 \tag{48}
\]
Let \(n\to\infty\), use (47), and then let \(L\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  We obtain
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n^{\diamond}
 \ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{49}
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix \(a>0\).  Attainment provides \(K^a\in\mathcal C_{\eta_0}\) such that
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_{r_0}}E_h\ell_0\{K^a(W_0)\}
 \le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a.
 \tag{50}
\]
Transfer \(K^a\) through Carter's forward kernel and the affine score map.  The completed-arrangement comparison pairs every \(u\in D_{n,v}\cap B_{k_n}\) with a Gaussian mean carrying label \(v\), and pairs every \(u\in H_{n,r_0}\cap B_{k_n}\) with a restored Gaussian mean in \(H_{r_0}\).  Equal-covariance translation, Carter total variation, covariance replacement, the active-boundary charge, and the restoration term are all included in \(\rho_n\).  Since coverage indicators and \(\ell_0\) take values in \([0,1]\), the transferred rule has window coverage at least \(1-\eta_0-\rho_n\) and window risk at most
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n.
 \tag{51}
\]

The algebra of \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) applies with both infima and suprema restricted to the same window.  Put
\[
 q_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
 \tag{52}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(\eta_0>0\), and
\[
 (1-q_n)(1-\eta_0-\rho_n)+q_n=1-\eta_0.
 \tag{53}
\]
Mixing with the full label set therefore produces a member of \(\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}^{\diamond}\).  Since \(0\le\ell_0\le1\), (51)--(53) give
\[
 M_n^{\diamond}
 \le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n
 +\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
 \tag{54}
\]
Let \(n\to\infty\), then \(a\downarrow0\), and combine (49) and (54):
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}M_n^{\diamond}
 =M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{55}
\]

Every globally honest rule is window-honest, and its global separated-risk supremum is at least its windowed supremum.  Directly from the two minimax definitions,
\[
 M_n\ge M_n^{\diamond}.
 \tag{56}
\]
Equations (55)--(56) prove
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
 \ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{57}
\]

If effective compatible density is affirmatively resolved, or a separate sufficient compatibility package is supplied, the abstract rule in (50) may be replaced by a finite CertGluePFL receipt; when the finite-window comparison enclosures are also supplied, its transfer and repair are replayable.  This conditional fact does not make the diagonal selection in (46) computable.  Finally, \(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\) exhibits arrays identical on every fixed compact but having different global upper minimax behavior.  Hence the stated compact premises cannot imply a global \(\limsup\), a globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal, or a two-sided global limit.
