Suppose \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  Then every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) has a compatible lift \(p_0+tBu\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) for all sufficiently small positive \(t\), admits a feasible optimal symbolic completion in \(\mathcal B_0\), and belongs to at least one completed semantic cell.  Hence
\[
 \bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d.
\]
Equality signs belong to all incident completions.  More generally, use the causally compatible offset space
\[
 \mathcal K_0=\{A_\Psi z:z\in\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\}.
\]
If \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\), the compact-uniform moving remainders vanish, and a compact \(C\) has distance at least \(\tau>0\) from every hyperplane \(c_j+a_j'u=0\), then the lawful multinomial label on \(C\) eventually equals the label generated by \(D_v^0(c)\).  At \(c=0\) this is the label fan of \(\mathfrak G_0\).  If there are no active cuts, there is one retained global semantic label and the honest diameter minimax value is zero.
statements.justification: The corrected proposition derives legal symbolic completions from the compatible observed-law polytope and a proved relative-interior lift.
statements.gap: Its proof can be attached after the new domain assumptions and structured definitions are adjudicated; no ambient-simplex neighborhood is used.
statements.consumer: It validates the global cover condition for the zero-offset Gaussian experiment and the causal moving-offset space.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(L=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  By
\(\text{ass:causal-base-relative-interior}\),
\(\text{ass:tangent-image-compatible}\), and
\(\text{lem:relative-interior-tangent-lift}\), for every
\(u\in\mathbb R^d\) there is \(t_u>0\) such that
\[
 p_0+tBu\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 \qquad(0<t\leq t_u).
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\text{lem:compatible-observed-law-polytope}\) and
\(\text{prop:fiber-polytope-equivalence}\), every law in (1) has a
nonempty finite response-type fiber, so all of the finitely many branch
operations and endpoint programs in \(\mathscr L_0\) admit feasible
optimal symbolic completions.

Choose a sequence \(t_k\downarrow0\).  Since the set of symbolic branch
and primal--dual optimal completions is finite, a subsequence has one
constant completion \(b\).  If
\(\psi(p)=\alpha_\psi'p+\beta_\psi\in\mathscr L_0\) and
\(\psi(p_0)\ne0\), continuity implies that the sign along this
subsequence is its frozen base sign.  If \(\psi(p_0)=0\), affinity gives
the exact identity
\[
 \psi(p_0+t_kBu)=t_k\alpha_\psi'Bu.
\tag{2}
\]
Consequently the constant completion chooses the weak tangent sign
prescribed by \(\alpha_\psi'Bu\).  If
\(\alpha_\psi'Bu=0\), both weak inequalities hold, which is precisely
the stipulated incidence convention.  Passing the finite weak linear
inequalities and the finite primal--dual feasibility and optimality
equalities to the limit shows that \(b\in\mathcal B_0\) is a feasible
optimal completion at \(u\).  Thus \(u\in P_{v,b}^0\) for the semantic
projection \(v\) of \(b\).  This is also the conclusion of
\(\text{lem:compatible-lift-completed-cover}\), and hence
\[
 \bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d.
\tag{3}
\]
Identity (2) proves directly that a zero tangent slack belongs to every
incident weak completion.

We next prove the moving-offset assertion.  Let \(A_\Psi\) be the
matrix with rows \(\alpha_j'\) for
\(j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\).  Since every active cut satisfies
\(\psi_j(p_0)=0\), the definition of \(c_n\) gives
\[
 c_n=\sqrt n\,A_\Psi\{p_n(0)-p_0\}.
\tag{4}
\]
By \(\text{ass:local-family-affine-hull}\), the vector in braces lies
in \(L\).  Therefore (4) proves
\(c_n\in A_\Psi L=\mathcal K_0\); offset compatibility is derived rather
than assumed.

Suppose now that \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\), that the moving
remainders converge uniformly on compact sets as stated, and that a
compact set \(C\) has positive distance from every hyperplane
\(c_j+a_j'u=0\).  When the active index set is nonempty, compactness,
finiteness, and the nonzero normal condition give
\[
 \delta_C
 :=\min_{u\in C}\min_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
       |c_j+a_j'u|>0.
\tag{5}
\]
When the active set is empty, the following sign argument is vacuous.
Convergence of \(c_n\) and compact-uniform convergence of the
remainders imply that, eventually,
\[
 \max_j|c_{n,j}-c_j|
 +\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|
 <\frac{\delta_C}{2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Using the defining identity
\[
 \zeta_{n,j}(u)=c_{n,j}+a_j'u+e_{n,j}(u),
\tag{7}
\]
the reverse triangle inequality and (5)--(6) show that
\(\zeta_{n,j}(u)\) and \(c_j+a_j'u\) have the same strict sign,
simultaneously for every \(u\in C\) and every active \(j\).

For completeness, if \(\psi(p_0)\ne0\), then
\(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\) and
\(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\) give
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\|p_n(u)-p_0\|_2
 \leq \|p_n(0)-p_0\|_2
 +n^{-1/2}\sup_{u\in C}\|Bu\|_2+o(n^{-1/2})
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus every nonzero base sign is also eventually its frozen sign,
uniformly on \(C\).  A zero-base cut with zero tangent normal is, by
\(\text{def:label-fan}\), a fixed tie included in all of its incident
completions.  The complete finite cut list therefore has exactly the
same branch signs for the multinomial rule and the offset arrangement
on \(C\).  By \(\text{def:multinomial-label-regions}\),
\[
 \mathcal V_n(u)=\{v:u\in D_v^0(c)\}
 \qquad\text{for every \(u\in C\)}
\tag{9}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The compact-domain lemma ensures
simultaneously that \(C\subseteq\mathcal U_n\), so every label on the
left side of (9) is lawful.

Finally suppose that
\(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}=\varnothing\).  Every retained tangent
cell is then all of \(\mathbb R^d\).  The equivalence step in the
definition of the semantic map identifies patterns with the same
completed tangent region and retains only one representative, so there
is one global semantic label, say \(v_0\).  The deterministic rule
reporting \(\{v_0\}\) has coverage one at every mean and
\(\ell(\{v_0\})=\delta(v_0,v_0)=0\).  Since diameter loss is
nonnegative, its honest minimax value is therefore zero.

statements.statement:
Under \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\), the globally completed active tangent arrangement has a full-dimensional strict chamber unless there are no active cuts, in which case its unique component is \(\mathbb R^d\).  The canonical search returns \(P_{v_*,b_*}^0\), a rational point \(u_*\), and exact rational linear-programming certificates such that \(\rho_0>0\).  With \(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\),
\[
 \{v:u_*\in D_v^0\}=\{v_*\},\qquad
 \inf_{v\ne v_*}\inf_{g\in D_v^0}
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}\ge r_0.
\]
Thus \(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\) for \(\mathfrak G_0\) without a causal margin assumption.
statements.justification: A strict chamber and its rational row-distance receipt now rest on causally legal tangent geometry.
statements.gap: The finite hyperplane and Mahalanobis calculations close after the corrected cover is applied.
statements.consumer: The receipt verifies the separated-domain premise before CertGluePFL is invoked.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume first that
\(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\ne\varnothing\).  Every active normal
\(a_j\) is a nonzero rational vector.  A finite union of the proper
hyperplanes \(\{u:a_j'u=0\}\) has empty interior, so its complement
contains a nonempty full-dimensional open chamber.  Rational points
are dense in that chamber.  By
\(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\), every point of the chamber
has a feasible optimal completion.  All active signs are constant on
the chamber, and the complete cut list includes every branch,
feasibility, optimality, and semantic assertion inequality.  Hence its
strict sign pattern determines one completed tangent component.
Patterns with identical completed regions have only their canonical
semantic representative.  It follows that the chamber is contained
in a unique semantic component \(P_{v,b}^0\).

Choose a rational point in this strict chamber.  Every nonredundant
defining inequality of its component has strictly positive rational
slack there.  The active arrangement is homogeneous, so multiplying
this point by a sufficiently large positive rational number makes
every such slack at least \(1\).  Therefore the rational linear
program used to define \(i_*\), which imposes
\(0\leq\gamma\leq1\), has optimum \(\gamma=1\) for at least one
component.  The canonical finite search consequently finds a positive
margin component and returns its lexicographically first rational
optimal basic solution \(u_*\).  This point is in a strict chamber of
the selected component.  If the active list is empty instead, the
prescribed choice \(u_*=0\) lies in the unique component
\(\mathbb R^d\).  In both cases, with
\(v_*=\operatorname{pr}_V(i_*)\),
\[
 \{v:u_*\in D_v^0\}=\{v_*\}.
\tag{10}
\]

Consider any retained rival component
\[
 P_{v,b}^0=\{g:A_{v,b}^0g\leq b_{v,b}^0\},
 \qquad v\ne v_*.
\tag{11}
\]
It cannot contain \(u_*\), by (10).  Since (11) is exactly the
intersection of its displayed closed halfspaces, at least one
displayed row \(i\) has the positive rational gap
\[
 \gamma_{v,b,i}
 :=(A_{v,b}^0u_*-b_{v,b}^0)_i>0.
\tag{12}
\]
That row is nonzero.  By \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), every
coordinate of \(p_0\) is positive; by the declared rank condition on
\(B\), \(Bx\ne0\) for \(x\ne0\).  Therefore
\[
 x'I_0x
 =x'B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}Bx
 =\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0
 \qquad(x\ne0).
\tag{13}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\).  In particular,
\(\|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}>0\).

For every \(g\in P_{v,b}^0\), its \(i\)-th inequality and (12) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \gamma_{v,b,i}
 &\leq (A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}(u_*-g)\\
 &\leq
 \|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}},
 \end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
where the second step is Cauchy--Schwarz after inserting
\(\Sigma_0^{1/2}\Sigma_0^{-1/2}\).  If the rational norm enclosure in
the certificate gives
\[
 s_{v,b,i}\geq
 \|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}>0,
\]
then (14), equivalently
\(\text{lem:violated-row-mahalanobis-separation}\), yields
\[
 \inf_{g\in P_{v,b}^0}
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \geq
 \frac{\gamma_{v,b,i}}{s_{v,b,i}}
 =\rho_{v,b}>0.
\tag{15}
\]
There are finitely many rival components.  Hence the minimum defining
\(\rho_0\) is positive; if there is no rival component, the included
value \(1\) gives \(\rho_0=1\).  Since
\(r_0=\min\{r_{\mathrm{req}},\rho_0\}\), taking the minimum in (15)
over the finitely many components of every rival semantic union gives
\[
 \inf_{v\ne v_*}\inf_{g\in D_v^0}
 \|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \geq\rho_0\geq r_0.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (10) and (16) show \(u_*\in H_{r_0}\), including the allowed
case \(r_0=0\).  The chamber search, linear programs, row gaps, and
finite minima use rational arithmetic.  Since \(\Sigma_0\) is rational
positive definite, a proposed rational upper enclosure \(s\) is
checked exactly by the rational inequality
\(s^2\geq (A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\Sigma_0
(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}'\), with positivity checked separately.
Thus all stated receipts are finite exact rational certificates, and
no causal margin assumption was used.

statements.statement: For every observed law \(p\), the latent laws induced by \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\) are exactly the members of \(\mathcal F(p)\). Thus \(\Xi(p)\) is nonempty whenever \(p=p(P_0)\) for some \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and no compatible law satisfying any declared restriction is omitted from the endpoint optimizations.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\). First let \(P\in\mathcal F(p)\). Because \(X\), both treatment responses, both selection responses, and both wage responses have finite support, the realized vector
\[
 R=\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1),S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1),Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)\}
\]
takes values in a finite set. No defiers puts its treatment coordinates in the declared monotone set. Conditional weak selection monotonicity puts every positive-mass complier type in \(\mathcal R_x\). Define \(\lambda_{xr}=P(X=x,R=r)\). Then \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}=1\).

Conditional randomization and the known assignment probabilities give
\[
 \begin{split}
 P(X=x,Z=z,D=d,S=s,Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=y)
 &=\bar\pi_z(x)\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_x}\lambda_{xr}
 \mathbf 1\{D_r(z)=d,S_r(d)=s,\\
 &\hspace{40mm}y=Y_r(d)\text{ if }s=1,\ 
 y=\dagger\text{ if }s=0\}\\
 &=(T_0\lambda)_{x,z,d,s,y}.
 \end{split}
\]
The three consistency assumptions justify these substitutions. Hence \(T_0\lambda=p\). Instrument--stratum positivity gives \(\sum_r\lambda_{xr}=P(X=x)\ge\pi_*\).

Dividing observed cells by \(\pi_z(x)>0\), then using randomization and consistency, shows
\[
 c_{axk}(p)=P\{X=x,D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),
 S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1,Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=y_k\}. \tag{3}
\]
For \(a=1\), subtraction cancels always-takers; for \(a=0\), the factor \(2a-1=-1\) reverses the subtraction and cancels never-takers. Summing (3) gives \(q_{ax}=P(X=x,\text{complier},S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1)\). Binary directional selection monotonicity then gives
\[
 m_x=\min(q_{0x},q_{1x})
 =P\{X=x,\text{complier},S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.
\]
Thus the final constraint in \(\Xi(p)\) is precisely aggregate target positivity, and \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\).

Conversely, let \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\). Draw \((X,R)\) with masses \(\lambda_{xr}\); conditional on \(X=x\), draw \(Z\) independently of \(R\) from \(\bar\pi_z(x)\); and set observed variables by the consistency maps. The support \(\mathcal R_x\) gives no defiers and complier-conditional selection monotonicity. The construction gives randomization and all consistency and exclusion restrictions. The inequalities in \(\Xi(p)\) give stratum and target positivity. Finally \(T_0\lambda=p\), so the law is in \(\mathcal F(p)\). The two constructions prove exact equivalence and the nonemptiness consequence.

statements.statement: For every observed law \(p=p(P_0)\) induced by some \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and every fixed \(t\in\mathcal T\), the lower construction returns one law \(P_t^-(p)\in\mathcal F(p)\) satisfying \(Q_{1,P_t^-(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p)}(t)=\underline\Delta(t;p)\). Both marginal quantiles in this equality are generated by the same compatible law.

statements.proof_tex:
By fiber--polytope equivalence, \(\Xi(p)\) is nonempty. It is a closed subset of a finite-dimensional probability simplex and hence compact. For \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\), let
\[
 H_a^\lambda(j)=\sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}
 \mathbf 1\{r\text{ is an always-selected complier},\ Y_r(a)\le y_j\},
 \qquad
 M^\lambda=\sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}\mathbf 1\{r\text{ is an always-selected complier}\}.
\]
The fiber constraint gives \(M^\lambda\ge m_*>0\). On the finite ordered grid,
\[
 Q_{a,P_\lambda}(t)=y_j
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 H_a^\lambda(j)\ge tM^\lambda
 \ \text{and}\ 
 [j=1\ \text{or}\ H_a^\lambda(j-1)<tM^\lambda]. \tag{4}
\]
All quantities are linear in \(\lambda\). For a fixed pair \((j_0,j_1)\), the common-slack program replaces each strict predecessor inequality by \(H_a^\lambda(j_a-1)\le tM^\lambda-\gamma\) and maximizes \(\gamma\). Its optimum is positive exactly when one \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\) realizes both quantiles in (4). Every \(\lambda\) realizes one of finitely many pairs, and every feasible pair is realized by its selected basic maximizer.

The effect takes values in the finite set \(\{y_{j_1}-y_{j_0}:1\le j_0,j_1\le J\}\). Choosing the feasible pair with smallest difference therefore equals the infimum over \(\Xi(p)\), and the selected maximizer induces one \(P_t^-(p)\in\mathcal F(p)\). Applying (4) to that same law in both arms gives
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^-(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p)}(t)=\underline\Delta(t;p).
\]

Both marginal quantiles in this equality are generated by the same compatible law.

statements.proof_tex:
The compactness and quantile characterization (4) in the lower-endpoint proof apply unchanged. The positive common-slack program for \((j_0,j_1)\) is feasible exactly when one \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\) realizes both grid quantiles. Selecting the feasible pair with largest \(y_{j_1}-y_{j_0}\), and then its lexicographically least positive-slack basic maximizer, produces one \(P_t^+(p)\in\mathcal F(p)\) satisfying
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^+(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p)}(t)
 =\max_{\lambda\in\Xi(p)}
 \{Q_{1,P_\lambda}(t)-Q_{0,P_\lambda}(t)\}
 =\overline\Delta(t;p).
\]
The maximum exists because this objective has finite range on the nonempty compact fiber.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) with observed law \(p=p(P)\), the displayed cell contrasts identify the selected-complier submeasures.  The capacity formulas give valid marginal outer bounds, while \(\underline\Delta(t;p)\) and \(\overline\Delta(t;p)\) are the separate same-law infimum and supremum over \(\mathcal F(p)\), attained by \(P_t^-(p)\) and \(P_t^+(p)\).  Moreover
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p)
 \subseteq
 \prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
 [\underline\Delta(t;p),\overline\Delta(t;p)],
\]
with no rectangle-equality claim.  For the tangent conclusion, fix \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), set \(p_0=p(P_0)\), and suppose
\[
 p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0).
\]
For rational \((p_0,B)\), the compatible-direction lift proves that freezing nonzero base signs and retaining the active cuts \(\alpha_\psi'Bu\) yields closed rational cells \(P_{v,b}^0\) covering \(\mathbb R^d\), covariance \(\Sigma_0=\{B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}B\}^{-1}\), a certified nonempty separated domain, and a sample-size-free \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\).  No vector \(p_0+Bu\) is treated as a probability law.
statements.justification: The theorem now uses the identical observed base \(p_0=p(P_0)\), preserves same-law endpoint semantics, and separates causal identification from tangent-domain conditions.

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), put \(p=p(P)\), and write
\[
 \mathsf C
 :=\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\},
 \qquad
 \mathsf A
 :=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.
\]
By known assignment probabilities, conditional randomization, and
treatment, selection, and outcome consistency, for
\(a,z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \frac{p_{x,z,a,1,y_k}}{\pi_z(x)}
 =
 P\{X=x,D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=a,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1,
       Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=y_k\}.
\tag{17}
\]
The division is valid because
\(\text{ass:instrument-stratum-positivity}\) gives
\(\pi_z(x)\geq\pi_*>0\).  With binary treatments,
\(\text{ass:no-defiers}\) implies the pointwise identities
\[
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}
 -\mathbf 1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\}
 =\mathbf 1_{\mathsf C},
\tag{18}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=0\}
 -\mathbf 1\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=0\}
 =\mathbf 1_{\mathsf C}.
\tag{19}
\]
Substituting (17)--(19) into the definition of \(c_{axk}(p)\) proves
the identifying equality
\[
 c_{axk}(p)
 =P\{X=x,\mathsf C,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1,
       Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=y_k\}.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus the selected-complier submeasure is identified from the observed
law; equation (20) is a consequence of the maintained restrictions,
not a definition of the causal quantity.

Within a stratum \(x\) having positive complier probability,
\(\text{ass:weak-selection-monotonicity}\) makes the two
selected-complier selection events nested.  If \(s(x)=1\), the event
\(\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\}\) is the smaller one; if \(s(x)=-1\), the
event \(\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\) is the smaller one.  The same
conclusion is trivial in a stratum with zero complier probability.
Summing (20) over \(k\) therefore gives
\[
 m_x=\min\{q_{0x},q_{1x}\}
 =P(X=x,\mathsf C,\mathsf A),
 \qquad
 M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(\mathsf C,\mathsf A)\geq m_*>0.
\tag{21}
\]
The final inequality is
\(\text{ass:aggregate-target-positivity}\); it is the positivity
condition that makes every conditional quantile below well defined.

For an arbitrary compatible law, define
\[
 R_{ax}(j)
 :=P\{X=x,\mathsf C,\mathsf A,
       Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)\leq y_j\}.
\tag{22}
\]
By (20), this measure is obtained from the selected-complier measure
of total mass \(q_{ax}\) by retaining a submeasure of total mass
\(m_x\).  At most \(q_{ax}-m_x\) units of its mass below \(y_j\) can
be deleted, and neither the retained mass below \(y_j\) nor its total
mass can exceed \(C_{ax}(j)\) and \(m_x\), respectively.  Hence
\[
 [C_{ax}(j)-q_{ax}+m_x]_+
 \leq R_{ax}(j)
 \leq\min\{m_x,C_{ax}(j)\},
\tag{23}
\]
or equivalently
\[
 L_{ax}(j)\leq R_{ax}(j)\leq U_{ax}(j).
\tag{24}
\]
Summing (24) over the finite set \(\mathcal X\), dividing by the
strictly positive \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) in (21), and applying the
finite-grid generalized inverse yields
\[
 Q_a^-(t)\leq Q_{a,P}(t)\leq Q_a^+(t)
 \qquad(a\in\{0,1\},\ t\in\mathcal T).
\tag{25}
\]
Indeed, the upper cumulative envelope \(U\) crosses the threshold no
later than the true cumulative distribution, while the lower envelope
\(L\) crosses no earlier.  The defining sets are nonempty because at
\(j=J\) both envelopes sum to \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and \(t<1\).
Thus (25) is an observed-law marginal outer bound; it does not identify
the two latent marginal quantiles separately.

By \(\text{prop:fiber-polytope-equivalence}\), optimization over
\(\Xi(p)\) neither adds nor omits a member of \(\mathcal F(p)\).
The lower- and upper-endpoint attainment propositions therefore give,
separately for every \(t\in\mathcal T\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{1,P_t^-(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p)}(t)
 &=\underline\Delta(t;p),\\
 Q_{1,P_t^+(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p)}(t)
 &=\overline\Delta(t;p),
 \end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
where both marginal quantiles on either line are generated by the same
compatible law.  For every \(P\in\mathcal F(p)\), the definitions of
infimum and supremum imply
\[
 \underline\Delta(t;p)
 \leq Q_{1,P}(t)-Q_{0,P}(t)
 \leq\overline\Delta(t;p).
\tag{27}
\]
Collecting (27) over the finite index set \(\mathcal T\) proves
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p)
 \subseteq
 \prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
 [\underline\Delta(t;p),\overline\Delta(t;p)].
\tag{28}
\]
Attainment in (26) is coordinatewise and may use different compatible
laws at different \(t\) and at the two endpoints.  Thus (28) is an
outer rectangle and no rectangle-equality assertion has been made.

For the tangent conclusion, fix \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\)
and use the identical observed base \(p_0=p(P_0)\).  Under
\(\text{ass:causal-base-relative-interior}\) and
\(\text{ass:tangent-image-compatible}\),
\(\text{lem:relative-interior-tangent-lift}\) proves that every
direction \(Bu\) has a compatible small positive lift; no ambient
simplex neighborhood is invoked.  The proposition
\(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\) then supplies closed rational
cells satisfying
\[
 \bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d.
\tag{29}
\]
Since \(p_0\in\Delta^\circ(\mathcal J)\) and \(B\) has column rank
\(d\), for every \(x\ne0\),
\[
 x'B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}Bx
 =\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0.
\tag{30}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\).  For rational
\((p_0,B)\), both \(I_0\) and \(\Sigma_0\) are rational.  Proposition
\(\text{prop:job-corps-radius-nonempty}\) supplies the certified point
\(u_*\in H_{r_0}\), so the separated domain is nonempty.

The finite rational component description and semantic projection in
\(\text{def:label-fan}\), the global cover (29), positive-definite
rational covariance (30), the declared finite rational metric and
honesty level, and the nonempty separated domain verify the respective
membership conditions for the sample-size-free encoded Gaussian
experiment.  Hence \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\).  Every tangent
inequality used here is the affine directional slack obtained from a
compatible lift at \(p_0\); at no point was \(p_0+Bu\) treated as a
probability law.

statements.statement:
Under the declared Job Corps assignment, support, randomization, consistency, no-defiers, complier-conditional selection-monotonicity, and \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\ge m_*>0\) restrictions, let \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), set \(p_0=p(P_0)\), and impose the declared relative-interior and tangent-image conditions.  The response-type fiber computes the separate same-law endpoints and proves
\[
\Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)
\subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
[\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)],
\]
with no rectangle-equality claim.  The completed tangent cells define a lawful \(\mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E\) with certified nonempty \(H_{r_0}\).  The fixed-base compact transfer has the linear Carter--geometry--covariance modulus in \(\text{thm:fixed-stratum-transfer}\), and the qualitative moving-offset comparison is unconditional for any supplied Gaussian rule.  Construction of a finite replayable moving-offset Gaussian rule is conditional on the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\), or on a separately proved sufficient compatibility package; replayable comparison accounting also requires the stated effective finite-window enclosures to be supplied.  Under zero-offset centering, the diagonally selected expanding lawful windows satisfy
\[
M_n^{\diamond}\to M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
\qquad
\liminf_nM_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\]
The restricted singleton-\(\mathcal X\), perfect-compliance, finite-wage-grid submodel in \(\text{prop:bffl-discrete-perfect-compliance-embedding}\) embeds the Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes always-employed comparison, but there is no unrestricted-class inclusion or automatic sharpness transfer.  No globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal, global \(\limsup_nM_n\), two-sided global multinomial minimax limit, or algorithmic diagonal-window selection is asserted.
statements.justification: The proposition retains exact same-law causal identification, lawful tangent geometry, compact transfer, and conditional replayable Gaussian certification.
statements.gap: A global unbounded sampled-data primal and global two-sided minimax convergence are no longer promised.
statements.consumer: The workflow supports simultaneous ordered-wage assertions with an expanding-window sampled-data receipt and no rectangle-equality overclaim.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: composition of exact finite-fiber identification, rational tangent geometry, compact experiment comparison, and a restricted published-model embedding.}

Let \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and \(p_0=p(P_0)\).  The known-assignment, stratum-positivity, conditional-randomization, three consistency, no-defiers, complier-conditional selection-monotonicity, and aggregate target-positivity assumptions are the separately declared restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  In particular,
\[
 M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\ge m_*>0,
 \tag{58}
\]
so every conditional always-selected-complier quantile used below has a positive denominator.

By \(\text{thm:causal-label-polyhedralization}\), the observed-cell contrasts identify the selected-complier submeasures and the finite response-type fiber is exactly the full compatible-law fiber.  For each fixed \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(\text{prop:lower-endpoint-attainment}\) and \(\text{prop:upper-endpoint-attainment}\) provide same-law witnesses satisfying
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)
 =\underline\Delta(t;p_0),
 \tag{59}
\]
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)
 =\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
 \tag{60}
\]
For any single \(P\in\mathcal F(p_0)\), the definitions of the infimum and supremum give
\[
 \underline\Delta(t;p_0)
 \le Q_{1,P}(t)-Q_{0,P}(t)
 \le\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
 \tag{61}
\]
Taking all \(t\) and all compatible \(P\) proves the outer bound
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)
 \subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
 [\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)].
 \tag{62}
\]
The witnesses in (59)--(60) may depend on both \(t\) and the selected endpoint.  Thus coordinatewise endpoint attainment does not prove equality in (62), and no Cartesian joint sharpness is asserted.

Under relative interiority and tangent-image compatibility, \(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\) gives
\[
 \bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d,
 \tag{63}
\]
with equality faces included in every incident label.  Because \(B\) has column rank \(d\) and \((p_0)_j\ge\kappa>0\), for every nonzero \(z\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 z'I_0z=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}
 \frac{\{(Bz)_j\}^2}{(p_0)_j}>0.
 \tag{64}
\]
Hence \(I_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\); rational \(p_0\) and \(B\) make \(\Sigma_0\) rational.  The exact violated-row construction in \(\text{prop:job-corps-radius-nonempty}\) gives
\[
 H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing.
 \tag{65}
\]
The finite rational completed cells, (63), (64), and (65) are respectively the encoding, cover, covariance, and nonempty-separated-domain requirements in \(\text{def:experiment-class}\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E.
 \tag{66}
\]

The proved \(\text{thm:fixed-stratum-transfer}\) supplies, on every eligible fixed compact \(C\), the explicit modulus
\[
 C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
 +(H_C+A_0)x_n(C)+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C),
 \tag{67}
\]
without assigning a root-\(n\) rate to its last two terms.  For moving offsets, \(\text{lem:moving-offset-carter-geometry}\) and \(\text{thm:moving-offset-transfer}\) give, for every supplied Gaussian rule on \(C\),
\[
 C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
 +\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 +(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C).
 \tag{68}
\]
Since \(c_n\to c\) and \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\to0\), the actual and rationalized offsets lie in one compact offset set, so the same finite \(H_C\) is valid in (68).  Taking \(\overline\chi_n=\chi_n\) proves qualitative compact convergence.  A finite replayable Gaussian rule in (68) exists only under the affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion, or under another sufficient compatibility package; effective rational upper bounds for \(d_n(C)\) and \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\) must separately be supplied for replayable comparison accounting.

Under zero-offset centering, \(\text{thm:compact-exhaustion-transfer}\) gives the diagonally selected expanding-window statements
\[
 M_n^{\diamond}\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
 \ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{69}
\]
Its proof selects windows by eventual compact inequalities and does not make that selection computable.  By \(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\), compact-uniform comparison alone cannot strengthen (69) to a global upper limit or to a globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal.

Finally, apply \(\text{prop:bffl-discrete-perfect-compliance-embedding}\).  On its singleton-\(\mathcal X\) restriction, perfect compliance gives
\[
 D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)
 \quad\text{almost surely},
 \tag{70}
\]
and \(s=+1\) turns monotone employment into the declared complier-conditional selection monotonicity.  If \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\), then
\[
 \{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),
 S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}=EE,
 \qquad
 M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\ge m_*>0.
 \tag{71}
\]
Known rational assignment probabilities with \(\bar\pi_z\ge\pi_*\), randomized treatment, and the finite wage-grid restriction supply the remaining declared requirements.  Hence that restricted induced law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  The proposition explicitly supplies no unrestricted-class inclusion and no automatic sharpness transfer outside this submodel.

If effective compatible density is affirmatively resolved, conditional \(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) applied to (66) yields the replayable Gaussian certificate.  Without that extra premise, (59)--(69) remain the unconditional same-law identification, rational tangent, fixed-compact transfer, moving-offset comparison for a supplied rule, and diagonal-window conclusions.  These are exactly the claims of the proposition.

statements.statement: For every external bounded experiment in \(\mathfrak E_K\), where \(K_{\mathrm{par}}\) is a nonempty compact rational polytope, \(D_v^K=D_v\cap K_{\mathrm{par}}\), and \(\bigcup_vD_v^K=K_{\mathrm{par}}\), define honesty over \(D_v^K\), separated risk over \(H_r^K\), and all parameter suprema only over \(K_{\mathrm{par}}\). Gaussian smoothing followed by rational gridding is dense for \(M_K(r)\), and outward finite-prior primal-dual programs converge to \(M_K(r)\) and terminate at every rational absolute accuracy. No recession chart, tangential average, incidence path, or recession-tail ledger is needed. This is a standalone bounded reduction and does not assert \(\mathfrak E_K\subseteq\mathfrak E\).
statements.justification: The external bounded class is the required sanity check against compact-parameter Gaussian decision theory without making an impossible global-cover claim for compact label regions.
statements.gap: This is a fidelity reduction to compact minimax confidence-set approximation, not a novelty claim and not a subclass relation to the unbounded experiment class.
statements.consumer: Compact composite-testing and minimax expected-size procedures provide regression tests for the core-only implementation in which the recession library is disabled.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an experiment in \(\mathfrak E_K\). The covariance is positive definite, \(K_{\mathrm{par}}\) is compact, the label regions cover it, and \(H_r^K\ne\varnothing\). Let \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta^K\) have risk at most \(M_K(r)+a\), where \(a>0\). Gaussian smoothing at scale \(s>0\) gives coverage at least \(1-\eta-t_s\) and risk at most \(M_K(r)+a+Dt_s\), where \(t_s=\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\}\).

Compactness gives \(R<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{h\in K_{\mathrm{par}}}P_h\{W\notin[-R,R]^d\}\le q.
\]
Replace the rule outside this box by \(V\); coverage cannot decrease and risk rises by at most \(Dq\). On the box, use a rational observation mesh of Mahalanobis diameter \(b\) and rational simplex rounding with \(L^1\)-error \(\zeta\). The smoothing modulus bounds every \([0,R_f]\)-valued expectation error by
\[
 R_f\left\{\frac12\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\frac b s+\zeta\right\}.
\]
Thus the finite rational rule has a computable coverage deficit \(\rho\to0\) and risk at most \(M_K(r)+a+o(1)\). Mixing with \(V\) with probability \(\rho/(\eta+\rho)\) restores exact honesty and adds at most \(D\rho/(\eta+\rho)\). Sending \(a,s,q,b,\zeta\) to zero proves density.

For lower bounds, repeat the finite-subcover and finite-dimensional separation proof of atomic duality with means restricted to \(D_v^K\) and \(H_r^K\). Every number below \(M_K(r)\) is exceeded by a finite-prior Lagrange dual. Hence finite-prior values converge upward and repaired gridded-primal values converge downward.

Gaussian probabilities of rational boxes are computable by truncating the exponential series with an explicit remainder. Suprema over the compact rational polytope are enclosed by a rational mean mesh and the Gaussian-shift modulus. Enumerate mesh, rounding, integration, and finite-prior precisions, retain outward endpoints, and stop at the first gap below the requested rational accuracy. Convergence proves termination. No recession object is used.

statements.statement: For \(\mathfrak G_4\) at \(r=2\), the exhibited rule \(Q_{49/25}\) is globally \(0.95\)-honest because \(2\Phi(-49/25)<0.049995791\), and \(\sup_{h\in H_2}E_h\ell\{Q_{49/25}(W)\}<3/4+\arctan(\sqrt{3/10})/(2\pi)-\{\Phi(1/25)-1/2\}<0.813799\). The exact atomic dual value \(L_4\) generated by \(\beta_4\) and \(\nu_4\) exceeds \(0.361100\); its whole-line scalar reduction charges less than \(3753/10^{15}\) for replacing the optimizing multiplier by \(\lambda_4\). At \(r=0\), common-contact coverage implies risk at least \(14/15\), and \(K_{\mathrm{ct}}\) attains \(14/15\).
statements.justification: Every numerical bound now names the exact rule, atoms, weights, analytic reduction, and outward replacement charge needed for reproduction.
statements.gap: No published paper studies this four-label fan, and the rigorous enclosure width remains \(0.452699\), far above the requested milliscale gap.
statements.consumer: The explicit formulas are mandatory regression objects for every implementation of the global certificate algorithm.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: standardized facet inequalities, an exact bivariate
Gaussian comparison, and pointwise finite-action dual minimization.}
Put
\[
 q=\frac{49}{25},\qquad k=\sqrt{\frac3{10}},\qquad
 s=\sqrt{\frac{13}{10}},
\]
and use the whitening map in
\(\mathrm{def:four\mbox{-}label\mbox{-}primal\mbox{-}object}\),
\[
 z=\left(\frac a{\sqrt{1/8}},\frac b{\sqrt{3/20}}\right).
\tag{1}
\]
Every row of every displayed \(F_v\) has Euclidean norm one.  If
\(h\in D_v\), both inward standardized facet means are nonnegative.
Therefore the union bound gives
\[
 P_h\{v\notin Q_q(W)\}\leq2\Phi(-q).
\tag{2}
\]
Outward rational evaluation gives
\[
 0.0249978951482
 <\Phi(-49/25)
 <0.0249978951483.
\tag{3}
\]
For clarity, all decimal endpoints in this proof denote the corresponding
terminating rationals.  A check of (3), and of the intervals below, uses
only rational arithmetic: enclose each displayed square root by squaring
rational endpoints; enclose \(\pi\) through the alternating Machin identity
\(\pi/4=4\arctan(1/5)-\arctan(1/239)\); range-reduce the exponential; and
integrate its alternating Taylor bounds on rational subintervals, with the
first omitted term charged outward.  Thus these are interval certificates,
not floating-point evaluations.  From (2)--(3),
\[
 2\Phi(-49/25)<0.0499957902966<\frac1{20},
\]
which proves global \(0.95\) coverage, including equality faces.

Now take \(h\in H_2\) with unique label \(v\).  In whitened coordinates the
other three cones form the complement of the interior of \(D_v\).
Consequently distance at least two from their union implies that each of
the two unit inward facet means of \(D_v\) is at least two.  If both observed
inward coordinates exceed \(q\), then \(v\) is included and every rival is
excluded by its opposite facet.  Hence \(Q_q(W)=\{v\}\) on that event.
The four possible correlations between the two inward noises are \(0\),
\(\sqrt{3/13}\), or \(-\sqrt{3/13}\), and so all are at least
\[
 \rho_*=-\sqrt{\frac3{13}}.
\tag{4}
\]
Let \(t=2-q=1/25\).  If \(\Phi_2(x,y;\rho)\) is the centered standard
bivariate Gaussian distribution function, differentiation under its
density integral and two integrations by parts give
\[
 \frac{\partial}{\partial\rho}\Phi_2(t,t;\rho)
 =\phi_2(t,t;\rho)>0.
\]
Thus correlation monotonicity and the preceding sufficient event imply
\[
 P_h\{Q_q(W)=\{v\}\}\geq\Phi_2(t,t;\rho_*).
\tag{5}
\]
Differentiating on the diagonal gives
\[
 \frac d{du}\Phi_2(u,u;\rho_*)
 =2\phi(u)\Phi\left(
 u\sqrt{\frac{1-\rho_*}{1+\rho_*}}\right)
 \geq\phi(u),\qquad u\geq0.
\tag{6}
\]
A direct polar-coordinate integration of the centered Gaussian quadrant
gives
\[
 \Phi_2(0,0;\rho_*)
 =\frac14+\frac{\arcsin(\rho_*)}{2\pi}
 =\frac14-\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}.
\tag{7}
\]
Integrating (6) from \(0\) to \(t\), using (5), and using
\(0\leq\ell\leq1\), yields
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_2}E_h\ell\{Q_q(W)\}
 \leq
 \frac34+\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}
 -\{\Phi(1/25)-1/2\}.
\tag{8}
\]
The rational interval procedure described after (3) gives
\[
 0.0797514300099
 <\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}
 <0.0797514300101
\tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 0.0159534368527
 <\Phi(1/25)-\frac12
 <0.0159534368530.
\tag{10}
\]
Substitution in (8) gives an upper bound below
\(0.8137979931574<0.813799\).

For the lower certificate, set
\(\mu_\pm=(\pm1/\sqrt2,2)\) and \(\mu_0=(0,2)\).
In whitened coordinates, \(\mu_+\) has distance exactly two from the rival
halfspace across \(a=0\), and distance greater than two from the lower
halfplane; hence \(\mu_+\in H_2\).  Symmetry gives \(\mu_-\in H_2\).
All three atoms have the same standardized second coordinate, so it
integrates out.  If \(z\) denotes the standardized first coordinate, the
risk-mixture density divided by \(\phi(z)\) is
\[
 \frac{\phi(z-2)+\phi(z+2)}{2\phi(z)}
 =e^{-2}\cosh(2z).
\tag{11}
\]
Under the discrete label metric, pointwise minimization in
\(\mathrm{def:four\mbox{-}label\mbox{-}dual\mbox{-}object}\) is exactly the
minimum of the risk-mixture density and \(\lambda\phi(z)\): reporting one
of the singletons \(02\) or \(12\) costs \(\lambda\phi(z)\), reporting an
action containing both costs the risk density, and every other action is
weakly more expensive.  Put
\[
 a_0=\frac{1028}{625},\qquad
 \lambda_0=e^{-2}\cosh(2a_0).
\tag{12}
\]
The two curves cross at \(\pm a_0\).  Integration on the central and two
outer intervals, followed by the penalty
\(2\eta\lambda_0=\lambda_0/10\), gives
\[
 D_0=
 \Phi(a_0-2)-\Phi(-a_0-2)
 +\lambda_0\{2\Phi(-a_0)-1/10\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Exact outward intervals are
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 1.8181887545408<\lambda_0<1.8181887545411,\\
 0.3612198823625<\Phi(a_0-2)<0.3612198823627,\\
 0.0001337999106<\Phi(-a_0-2)<0.0001337999108,\\
 0.0500055310938<\Phi(-a_0)<0.0500055310941.
 \end{gathered}
\tag{14}
\]
Rational substitution in (13) yields
\[
 D_0>0.3611061955936.
\]
For two multipliers, pointwise Lipschitz continuity of the minimum and the
penalty term imply
\[
 |D(\lambda)-D(\lambda')|
 \leq |\lambda-\lambda'|+\frac1{10}|\lambda-\lambda'|
 =\frac{11}{10}|\lambda-\lambda'|.
\tag{15}
\]
The first line of (14) and
\(\lambda_4=90909437727/50000000000\) make the right side of (15) less
than \(3753/10^{15}\).  Therefore
\[
 L_4=D(\lambda_4)>0.3611061955898>0.361100.
\tag{16}
\]
The support checks above and
\(\mathrm{thm:attainment\mbox{-}atomic\mbox{-}duality}\) make this a valid
minimax lower certificate.

Finally set \(r=0\).  All four closed regions contain the origin.  Global
honesty therefore implies
\[
 E_0|K(W)|=\sum_{v\in V_4}P_0\{v\in K(W)\}
 \geq4(1-1/20)=\frac{19}{5}.
\tag{17}
\]
For every \(A\subseteq V_4\),
\[
 |A|\leq1+3\mathbf1\{|A|\geq2\},
\tag{18}
\]
and, for the discrete metric, \(\ell(A)=\mathbf1\{|A|\geq2\}\).
Thus (17)--(18) imply
\(E_0\ell\{K(W)\}\geq14/15\).  Gaussian \(L^1\)-translation continuity,
as proved in (15) of the atomic-duality proof, makes
\(h\mapsto E_h\ell\{K(W)\}\) continuous.  Unique-label points of \(H_0\)
in each cone approach the origin, so \(R_0(K)\geq14/15\).
The rule \(K_{\mathrm{ct}}\) includes each label with probability
\(14/15+1/60=19/20\), and has loss one only when it reports \(V_4\), an
event of probability \(14/15\).  By
\(\mathrm{def:four\mbox{-}label\mbox{-}contact\mbox{-}object}\), it is
globally honest and attains \(14/15\).  This completes all parts of the
proposition.

statements.statement:
Under \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\), and \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), for every rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 \max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\longrightarrow0,
\]
with the maximum interpreted as zero when \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}=\varnothing\), and
\[
 \left[B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B\right]^{-1}\longrightarrow
 \Sigma_0.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\psi_j(p)=\alpha_j'p+\beta_j\).  Affinity and the definition of the moving remainder give the exact identity
\[
 e_{n,j}(u)=\alpha_j'
 \left(\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right).
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\) is finite, Cauchy--Schwarz implies, for every rational compact polytope \(C\),
\[
 \max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|
 \leq\left(\max_j\|\alpha_j\|_2\right)
 \sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n[\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}]-Bu\right\|_2
 \longrightarrow0
\tag{2}
\]
by the compact-uniform local-expansion assumption.  When the active set is empty, the maximum is zero by convention.

Base convergence and \(\min_j(p_0)_j\geq\kappa>0\) imply that every coordinate of \(p_n(0)\) is eventually at least \(\kappa/2\).  Coordinatewise reciprocal is continuous on that set, and therefore
\[
 B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B
 \longrightarrow B'\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1}B=I_0.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(x\ne0\), full column rank of \(B\) and positivity of \(p_0\) give
\[
 x'I_0x=\|\operatorname{diag}(p_0)^{-1/2}Bx\|_2^2>0.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(I_0\) is positive definite.  Matrix inversion is continuous on the positive-definite cone, so (3)--(4) and \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\) yield
\[
 [B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B]^{-1}\longrightarrow\Sigma_0.
\tag{5}
\]

statements.statement:
Let
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 =\left\{\lambda\ge0:
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_x}\lambda_{xr}=1,
 \ \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_x}\lambda_{xr}\ge\pi_*\ \forall x,
 \ \sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}
 \mathbf 1\{D_r(1)>D_r(0),S_r(0)=S_r(1)=1\}\ge m_*
 \right\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 =T_0\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 =\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal J):\Xi(q)\ne\varnothing\}
 =\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal J):\mathcal F(q)\ne\varnothing\}.
\]
It is a rational polytope. Exact rational elimination first decides whether it is empty.  When it is nonempty, the finite rational response-type data yield an irredundant relative representation
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\{q:Eq=e,\ F_iq\le f_i,\ i\in I\},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{aff}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})=\{q:Eq=e\},
\]
and therefore certify \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\) by exact rational linear programming and row-space arithmetic.
statements.proof_tex:
The technique is finite response-type projection followed by exact rational polyhedral elimination.  Remove the equation \(T_0\lambda=p\) from the definition of \(\Xi(p)\); the remaining constraints are exactly those defining \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  Consequently, for every \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\),
\[
 \Xi(q)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\lambda\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\text{ with }T_0\lambda=q
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q\in T_0\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}. \tag{1}
\]
The already established response-type fiber equivalence gives
\[
 \Xi(q)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal F(q)\ne\varnothing. \tag{2}
\]
Equations (1) and (2), together with the definition of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), prove all three set equalities.

All coefficients in \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and \(T_0\) are rational.  Nonnegativity and unit total mass imply \(0\le\lambda_{xr}\le1\), so \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) is bounded; it is closed because it is the intersection of finitely many closed rational half-spaces and hyperplanes.  Moreover, because \(\bar\pi_0(x)+\bar\pi_1(x)=1\),
\[
 \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}(T_0\lambda)_j
 =\sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}\sum_{z=0}^1\bar\pi_z(x)=1,
\]
and every coordinate of \(T_0\lambda\) is nonnegative.  Eliminate the finitely many coordinates of \(\lambda\) from
\[
 \lambda\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}},\qquad q=T_0\lambda
\]
by successive pairwise inequality elimination.  To verify exactness of one step, isolate a coordinate \(x\) and write its constraints as
\[
 \ell_s(y)\le x\quad(s\in S),\qquad
 x\le u_t(y)\quad(t\in T),\qquad
 g_k(y)\le0\quad(k\in K),
\]
where all displayed functions are rational affine functions.  Such an \(x\) exists exactly when
\[
 \ell_s(y)\le u_t(y)\quad\forall(s,t)\in S\times T,
 \qquad g_k(y)\le0\quad\forall k\in K;
\]
if \(S\) or \(T\) is empty, choose \(x\) beyond the finitely many one-sided bounds.  Thus one step is equivalent to finitely many rational inequalities.  Iteration gives a finite rational system for \(T_0\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  The image is bounded because \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\).  Hence \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) is a rational polytope.

The same elimination decides emptiness.  Conditional on nonemptiness, redundancy of any output inequality is decided by maximizing its rational left-hand side subject to the other rational constraints.  Gaussian elimination applied to the equalities that hold throughout the resulting polytope gives rational matrices \(E,e\) with affine hull \(Eq=e\); the remaining nonredundant inequalities are the relative facets \(F_iq\le f_i\).  Hence
\[
 p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 Ep_0=e\ \text{ and }\ F_ip_0<f_i\ \forall i\in I. \tag{3}
\]
Moreover
\[
 \operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)=\ker E,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad EB=0. \tag{4}
\]
Every comparison in (3) and every equality in (4) is exact rational arithmetic.  This proves the certification claim.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  For every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) there is \(t_u>0\) such that
\[
 p_0+tBu\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 \qquad\text{for every }0\le t\le t_u.
\]
For rational \(u\), a positive rational \(t_u\) is computable from the rational relative-facet representation, and for every rational \(t\in[0,t_u]\) a rational response-type lift \(\lambda(t,u)\in\Xi(p_0+tBu)\) is computable.  Thus every tangent direction has a compatible full-law lift; feasibility is derived and is not assumed on an ambient simplex neighborhood.
statements.proof_tex:
Use the rational relative representation from the compatible-observed-law-polytope lemma,
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\{q:Eq=e,\ F_iq\le f_i,\ i\in I\}.
\]
Put \(L=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)=\ker E\) and \(v=Bu\).  The image condition gives \(v\in L\), hence
\[
 E(p_0+tv)=Ep_0+tEv=e \qquad(t\in\mathbb R). \tag{5}
\]
Relative interior gives a strictly positive slack
\[
 \gamma_i=f_i-F_ip_0>0\qquad(i\in I). \tag{6}
\]
With the minimum over an empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\), define
\[
 t_u=\min\left\{1,\ \min_{i:F_iv>0}\frac{\gamma_i}{2F_iv}\right\}>0. \tag{7}
\]
If \(0\le t\le t_u\) and \(F_iv>0\), then (6)--(7) give
\[
 F_i(p_0+tv)
 =f_i-\gamma_i+tF_iv
 \le f_i-\frac{\gamma_i}{2}<f_i. \tag{8}
\]
If \(F_iv\le0\), then
\[
 F_i(p_0+tv)\le F_ip_0=f_i-\gamma_i<f_i. \tag{9}
\]
Equations (5), (8), and (9) prove \(p_0+tBu\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  By the defining equality \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\{q:\mathcal F(q)\ne\varnothing\}\) and the established fiber-polytope equivalence, there exists \(\lambda(t,u)\in\Xi(p_0+tBu)\), and its response-type construction induces a law in \(\mathcal F(p_0+tBu)\).  When \(u\) and \(t\) are rational, all constraints have rational coefficients, and exact rational linear programming returns a basic feasible \(\lambda(t,u)\).  Formula (7) supplies the computable rational upper step.  This is the promised computable lift.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\), \(p_n(0)\to p_0\),
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2\to0
 \quad\text{for every compact }C\subset\mathbb R^d,
\]
and \(p_n(u)-p_0\in\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\) for every \((n,u)\).  Then every compact \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) is contained in \(\mathcal U_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  By relative interior, there is \(r_{\mathrm{rel}}>0\) such that
\[
 \{p_0+z:z\in L,\ \|z\|_2\le r_{\mathrm{rel}}\}
 \subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}. \tag{10}
\]
Fix a compact \(C\).  The local expansion and boundedness of \(B C\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{u\in C}\|p_n(u)-p_0\|_2
 &\le \|p_n(0)-p_0\|_2
   +n^{-1/2}\sup_{u\in C}\|Bu\|_2\\
 &\quad+n^{-1/2}\sup_{u\in C}
 \left\|\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu\right\|_2
 \longrightarrow0.
 \end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
The affine-hull condition places every difference in (11) in \(L\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), (11) is at most \(r_{\mathrm{rel}}\); (10) then implies \(p_n(u)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) for every \(u\in C\).  The corrected definition of \(\mathcal U_n\) therefore gives \(C\subseteq\mathcal U_n\).

statements.statement:
Let \(0\le\rho<1\), and let \(\widetilde K\) be a randomized rule satisfying
\[
 \inf_{v\in V}\inf_{h\in D_v}P_h\{v\in\widetilde K(W)\}
 \ge1-\eta-\rho.
\]
Set \(q=\rho/(\eta+\rho)\), and let \(K^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho}(\widetilde K)\).  Then \(K^+\in\mathcal C_\eta\), and
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_r}E_h\ell\{K^+(W)\}
 \le
 \sup_{h\in H_r}E_h\ell\{\widetilde K(W)\}
 +\frac{D\rho}{\eta+\rho}.
\]

Suppose \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\).  Under the completed branch construction in \(\mathcal B_0\), every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) belongs to some feasible optimal tangent cell \(P_{v,b}^0\).  Consequently,
\[
 \bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
The technique is a finite active-set stability argument applied to the compatible convex-polyhedral lift.  Fix \(u\in\mathbb R^d\).  The relative-interior tangent-lift lemma supplies \(t_u>0\) such that
\[
 q_t=p_0+tBu\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}
 \qquad(0<t\le t_u). \tag{15}
\]
By the compatible-polytope representation and fiber equivalence, \(\Xi(q_t)\ne\varnothing\).  The feasible response weights satisfy \(0\le\lambda_{xr}\le1\) and finitely many closed linear constraints; hence \(\Xi(q_t)\) is compact.  Each separate endpoint program therefore has a primal optimizer.  To expose the dual step, write any fixed branch program as
\[
 \max_x c'x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Gx\le g,\ Hx=h. \tag{16}
\]
At a maximizer \(x_*\), let \(I\) index its active inequalities.  There is no direction \(d\) satisfying \(G_Id\le0\), \(Hd=0\), and \(c'd>0\), because a sufficiently small positive step from \(x_*\) would otherwise remain feasible and increase (16).  Applying the same finite pairwise linear-inequality elimination used above to this infeasible direction system yields multipliers \(y_I\ge0\) and \(z\) such that
\[
 c=G_I'y_I+H'z. \tag{17}
\]
Extend \(y_I\) by zeros off \(I\).  Then every feasible \(x\) obeys
\[
 c'x=y'Gx+z'Hx\le y'g+z'h,
\]
while equality holds at \(x_*\) because \(y_i(G_ix_*-g_i)=0\).  Hence \((y,z)\) is a dual optimizer.  Every endpoint value is finite because the wage grid is finite.  Thus at least one primal--dual feasible optimal branch completion exists at \(q_t\).

There are finitely many cuts \(\psi(p)=\alpha_\psi'p+\beta_\psi\).  If \(\psi(p_0)\ne0\), continuity of the affine map gives \(t_\psi>0\) for which
\[
 \operatorname{sign}\{\psi(q_t)\}=\operatorname{sign}\{\psi(p_0)\}
 \qquad(0<t<t_\psi). \tag{18}
\]
If \(\psi(p_0)=0\), then exactly
\[
 \psi(q_t)=t\alpha_\psi'Bu. \tag{19}
\]
Choose \(t>0\) below \(t_u\) and all the finitely many positive bounds in (18).  Select one feasible optimal completion at \(q_t\).  Equations (18)--(19) show that it agrees with every frozen base sign and with the weak tangent sign selected by \(u\).  If \(\alpha_\psi'Bu=0\), the equality-face convention places the cut in every incident completion.  Therefore this completion is one of the retained elements \(b\in\mathcal B_0\).  Its semantic assertion pattern has some retained representative \(v\in V\), and the same weak signs state precisely that
\[
 u\in P_{v,b}^0\subseteq D_v^0. \tag{20}
\]
Because \(u\) was arbitrary, (20) proves the asserted global cover.  Notice that (15), rather than feasibility of every ambient neighboring simplex law, is the only lawfulness step.

statements.statement:
Let \(\Sigma_0=\Sigma_0'\succ0\), let \(P_{v,b}^0=\{g:A_{v,b}^0g\le b_{v,b}^0\}\), let \(u_*\in\mathbb R^d\), and suppose row \(i\) has gap
\[
 \gamma=(A_{v,b}^0u_*-b_{v,b}^0)_i>0.
\]
If \(s\ge\|(A_{v,b}^0)_{i\cdot}\|_{\Sigma_0}>0\), then
\[
 \inf_{g\in P_{v,b}^0}\|u_*-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \ge \frac{\gamma}{s}>0.
\]

Let \(m\ge 2\), \(n\ge 1\), \(R\ge 1\), and
\[
 \Theta_R=\left\{\theta\in(0,1)^m:\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i=1,
 \ \frac{\max_i\theta_i}{\min_i\theta_i}\le R\right\}.
\]
For \(P_\theta=\operatorname{Multinomial}(n,\theta)\) and the matched Gaussian law
\(Q_\theta=N_m\{n\theta,n(\operatorname{diag}\theta-\theta\theta')\}\), there is a constant \(C_R\), depending only on \(R\), and parameter-independent Markov kernels in both directions such that both uniform total-variation errors are at most
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car}}(n,m,R)=C_R\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Equivalently, the Le Cam distance between \(\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_R\}\) and \(\{Q_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_R\}\) is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car}}(n,m,R)\).

statements.justification: This is the exact published comparison substrate used for fixed positive-cell multinomial experiments.
statements.gap: The source compares statistical experiments only; it does not compare causal truth regions or control escaping parameters.
statements.consumer: The fixed-compact transfer applies these kernels before separately charging score, covariance, and semantic-boundary errors.

statements.statement:
Put \(m=|\mathcal J|\). Under \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\), and \(\text{ass:multinomial-local-expansion}\), for every compact \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) there is \(n_C\) such that
\[
 \min_{u\in C}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\ge \kappa/2,
 \qquad
 \frac{\max_jp_{n,j}(u)}{\min_jp_{n,j}(u)}\le 2/\kappa
 \quad(n\ge n_C).
\]
Consequently Carter's two kernels apply uniformly to \(\{p_n(u):u\in C\}\) with error
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{m\log m}{\sqrt n}.
\]
The same bound holds after any fixed measurable score or whitening map.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(M_C=\sup_{u\in C}\|u\|_2<\infty\), and write
\[
 r_n(u)=\sqrt n\{p_n(u)-p_n(0)\}-Bu.
\]
The local expansion gives \(\sup_{u\in C}\|r_n(u)\|_2\to0\). Hence
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\|p_n(u)-p_0\|_\infty
 \le \|p_n(0)-p_0\|_2+
 \frac{\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}M_C+\sup_{u\in C}\|r_n(u)\|_2}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
by \(\text{ass:multinomial-base-convergence}\). Since \(\min_j(p_0)_j\ge\kappa\) by \(\text{ass:multinomial-interior}\), the first displayed inequality follows eventually. Every probability coordinate is at most one, so the ratio is at most \(1/(\kappa/2)=2/\kappa\). Apply \(\text{thm:carter-positive-multinomial-gaussian-comparison}\) with \(R=2/\kappa\). Finally, if \(S\) is a measurable map and \(\mu,\nu\) are probability measures, then
\[
 \|S_\#\mu-S_\#\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\sup_B|\mu(S^{-1}B)-\nu(S^{-1}B)|
 \le \|\mu-\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}},
\]
which proves the score-map assertion.
statements.justification: It converts the abstract bounded-ratio premise into the displayed fixed-support compact positive-cell bound.
statements.gap: Carter does not perform this specialization to the local causal chart.
statements.consumer: Both compact transfer theorems use the resulting symbolic Carter error.

statements.statement:
Let \(\{P_\theta\}\) and \(\{Q_\theta\}\) be experiments with the same parameter set, and let \(T\) be a parameter-independent Markov kernel satisfying
\(\sup_\theta\|TP_\theta-Q_\theta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\epsilon\). If \(K\) is a randomized rule with actions in \(\mathcal A\), then \(K\circ T\) satisfies, for every \(v\in V\),
\[
 \sup_\theta\left|P_\theta\{v\in(K\circ T)(X)\}
 -Q_\theta\{v\in K(Y)\}\right|\le\epsilon,
\]
and for every \(g:\mathcal A\to[0,R]\),
\[
 \sup_\theta\left|E_{P_\theta}g\{(K\circ T)(X)\}
 -E_{Q_\theta}g\{K(Y)\}\right|\le R\epsilon.
\]
In particular the normalized Job Corps diameter loss has error at most \(\epsilon\), and a diameter loss bounded by \(D\) has error at most \(D\epsilon\).
statements.proof_tex:
For a fixed \(\theta\), composing \(T\) with \(K\) is another Markov kernel, so total variation contracts:
\[
 \|(K\circ T)P_\theta-KQ_\theta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \|TP_\theta-Q_\theta\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\epsilon.
\]
Apply the defining variational inequality for total variation first to the event \(\{A:v\in A\}\). For \(0\le g\le R\), the layer-cake identity gives
\[
 E_\mu g-E_\nu g
 =\int_0^R\{\mu(g>t)-\nu(g>t)\}\,dt,
\]
and therefore \(|E_\mu g-E_\nu g|\le R\|\mu-\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\). Taking \(g=\ell_0\), whose range is \([0,1]\), or \(g=\ell\), whose range is \([0,D]\), gives the last assertions.
statements.justification: This is the exact bridge from experiment comparison to coverage and bounded diameter loss.
statements.gap: It deliberately makes no assertion about changing truth regions.
statements.consumer: Fixed, moving-offset, and dual-certificate transfer all invoke it.

statements.statement:
The common-ray Følner operators commute. For every chain \(\tau\preceq\sigma\),
\[
 q_{\sigma,L}
 =\left(\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)}
 \mathsf A_{\varrho,L}\right)q_{\tau,L},
\]
and the transition operator is independent of the incidence path. If \(a\ge0\), \(\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\), and \(q_s(w)\) is an action-probability vector, then
\[
 \|q_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-q_{\sigma,L}(w)\|_1
 \le 2\min\{1,a/L\}.
\]
For every \(f:\mathcal A\to[0,R_f]\), the corresponding scalar bound is \(R_f\min\{1,a/L\}\). Shared face vertices have exactly identical traces under the global finite-element discretization. These identities give computable \(O(L^{-1})\) translation boundary ratios, but do not assert that \(q_{\sigma,L}=q_{\tau,L}\) on a shared face.
statements.proof_tex:
For two rays \(\varrho_1,\varrho_2\), Tonelli's theorem applies coordinatewise because every coordinate of a Markov kernel is nonnegative and bounded by one. Thus
\[
 \mathsf A_{\varrho_1,L}\mathsf A_{\varrho_2,L}q(w,A)
 =\frac1{L^2}\int_0^L\int_0^L
 q(w+t_1\varrho_1+t_2\varrho_2,A)\,dt_2dt_1
 =\mathsf A_{\varrho_2,L}\mathsf A_{\varrho_1,L}q(w,A).
\]
Induction over the finite ray set proves commutativity. Cancelling the literally shared factors in \(\mathscr R(\tau)\subseteq\mathscr R(\sigma)\) gives the displayed face-transition identity; commutativity makes the product, and hence every composite transition, independent of the chosen chain.

Write \(q=\mathsf A_{\sigma\setminus\{\varrho\},L}q_s\). For \(0\le a\le L\),
\[
 \mathsf A_{\varrho,L}q(w+a\varrho)-\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}q(w)
 =\frac1L\left\{\int_L^{L+a}q(w+t\varrho)\,dt-
 \int_0^aq(w+t\varrho)\,dt\right\}.
\]
Since an action-probability vector has \(\ell^1\)-norm one, the triangle inequality gives \(2a/L\). The trivial distance bound two handles \(a>L\). If \(F_q^f=\sum_Af(A)q_A\in[0,R_f]\), the difference of the two boundary integrals is at most \(R_fa\), giving \(R_fa/L\), with the trivial bound \(R_f\) for \(a>L\). Finally, a global simplicial complex identifies a geometric face vertex only once; using one variable at that vertex makes all incident affine traces equal there by the uniqueness of barycentric interpolation on the face. This last assertion is algebraic and does not identify the cone-interior averages with one another.
statements.justification: It proves the path-independent algebra and the uniform boundary ratio supplied by literally shared ray factors.
statements.gap: Commuting factors alone do not prove equality between a face rule and an incident cone rule.
statements.consumer: The effective-compatible-density target uses it as the strongest established simultaneous-incidence ingredient.

statements.statement:
For the finite completed affine arrangement defining \(D_v^0(c)\), fix compact sets \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) and \(C_c\subset\mathcal K_0\). There is a finite computable constant \(H(C,C_c)\) with the following property. If \(c,\widehat c\in C_c\), every active affine inequality is perturbed by at most \(\delta\), and \(u\in C\) has semantic label \(v\) in the perturbed completed system, then there is \(\bar u\in D_v^0(\widehat c)\) such that
\[
 \|u-\bar u\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \le H(C,C_c)\{\delta+\|c-\widehat c\|_\infty\}.
\]
Equality faces retain all incident labels. The same finite enumeration gives directed Hausdorff bounds for rival semantic unions and hence changes every separation distance by at most twice the displayed quantity. All constants are obtained by rational active-set enumeration and outward enclosure of \(\Sigma_0\)-norms.
statements.proof_tex:
Each completed branch is a finite weak system
\[
 A_bu\le \beta_b+G_bc,
\]
with rational \(A_b,\beta_b,G_b\). For a nonempty system, projection of \(u\) onto it and the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker equations show that the residual is generated by a linearly independent subset \(I\) of active row normals. Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \bigl(u,\{x:A_bx\le\beta_b+G_b\widehat c\}\bigr)
 \le H_b\bigl\|(A_bu-\beta_b-G_b\widehat c)_+\bigr\|_\infty,
\]
where one may take \(H_b\) to be the maximum, over the finitely many linearly independent row subsets \(I\), of an outward rational enclosure of the norm of the corresponding right inverse in the \(\Sigma_0^{-1}\) metric. This is a direct finite active-set proof of the linear error bound.

If \(u\) satisfies the system with right-hand perturbation \(r_b\), \(\|r_b\|_\infty\le\delta\), at offset \(c\), then
\[
 \bigl\|(A_bu-\beta_b-G_b\widehat c)_+\bigr\|_\infty
 \le \delta+\|G_b\|_{\infty\to\infty}\|c-\widehat c\|_\infty.
\]
Empty systems are discarded. When a system becomes feasible only at a boundary value of the offset, its limiting weak equalities occur in every incident completion by construction, so the same point is assigned the same semantic label in at least one retained incident system. Taking the maximum over finitely many branches, offset cells, and semantic labels, and enlarging it to absorb \(\|G_b\|_{\infty\to\infty}\), gives \(H(C,C_c)\). Applying the point-to-set bound in both directions to every component of a rival semantic union yields directed Hausdorff error at most the displayed bound. The inequality
\[
 |\operatorname{dist}(u,E)-\operatorname{dist}(\bar u,\bar E)|
 \le \|u-\bar u\|+d_{\mathrm H}(E,\bar E)
\]
then gives the factor two for separation distances. Rational active sets are finite, and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), so all inverses used on their ranks and all metric norms have terminating outward rational enclosures.
statements.justification: Finite rational active-set enumeration turns moving slack errors into explicit semantic and separation displacements.
statements.gap: This geometric perturbation result is separate from Carter's statistical comparison.
statements.consumer: The fixed and moving-offset transfers use its computable Hoffman constants.

statements.statement: Compact-uniform local expansion does not determine an unbounded-parameter minimax value. Specifically, for every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\) there are two two-category, two-label multinomial triangular arrays with the same positive base \(p_0\), the same full-rank tangent \(B\), and identical laws on every fixed compact for all sufficiently large \(n\), such that their zero-offset Gaussian tangent experiment has one semantic label and minimax diameter zero, whereas the second array has global honest diameter minimax value at least \(1-2\eta\) for every \(n\). Thus compact comparison cannot imply a global minimax upper bound without an expanding-domain or recession-control premise.
statements.proof_tex:
Take two categories, labels \(V=\{0,1\}\), discrete label metric, \(p_0=(1/4,3/4)\), and \(B=(1/16,-1/16)'\). For \(q\in(0,1)\), assign truth \(\{0\}\) when \(q<1/2\), truth \(\{0,1\}\) when \(q=1/2\), and truth \(\{1\}\) when \(q>1/2\). This is a completed rational polyhedral label map on the one-dimensional probability simplex. Let
\[
 q_n^A(u)=\frac14+\frac1{16}\operatorname{clip}(u/\sqrt n,-1,1),
 \qquad p_n^A(u)=(q_n^A(u),1-q_n^A(u)).
\]
Define \(p_n^B=p_n^A\) outside \(|u-n|\le\sqrt n\), while on that interval put
\[
 q_n^B(u)=\frac12+\frac{u-n}{8\sqrt n},
 \qquad p_n^B(u)=(q_n^B(u),1-q_n^B(u)).
\]
All coordinates of both arrays are at least \(3/16\). For every fixed compact \(C\), eventually \(C\cap[n-\sqrt n,n+\sqrt n]=\varnothing\) and clipping is inactive on \(C\). Therefore both arrays agree on \(C\) and
\[
 \sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n^A(u)-p_0\}-Bu\right\|_2
 =\sup_{u\in C}\left\|\sqrt n\{p_n^B(u)-p_0\}-Bu\right\|_2=0.
\]
They have the same base, tangent, information, covariance, and every fixed-compact limiting label. Because \(q_n^A(u)\le5/16<1/2\), its sole truth is label zero; the constant action \(\{0\}\) is honest and has diameter zero.

For the second array, \(q_n^B(n)=1/2\). At this parameter, honesty of any rule \(K_n\) implies
\[
 P_{1/2}\{0\in K_n\}\ge1-\eta,
 \qquad P_{1/2}\{1\in K_n\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
The union bound therefore gives
\[
 P_{1/2}\{K_n=\{0,1\}\}
 \ge1-2\eta.
\]
With the discrete metric, the expected diameter is precisely the probability of reporting \(\{0,1\}\). For every fixed randomized rule on the finite count space this probability is a polynomial, hence continuous, in \(q\). Parameters \(u=n+t\), \(t\ne0\), have a unique truth and converge to the boundary law as \(t\to0\). For separation radius zero they belong to the risk domain. Thus
\[
 \sup_{u:\,\mathcal V_n(u)\text{ is a singleton}}
 E_{p_n^B(u)}\ell\{K_n(N_n)\}
 \ge1-2\eta.
\]
Taking the infimum over globally honest \(K_n\) proves the asserted lower bound. The inserted boundary escapes to \(u_n=n\), so no fixed-compact hypothesis detects it.
statements.justification: This explicit witness tests and falsifies the attempted passage from compact comparison to a global minimax upper bound.
statements.gap: Compact LAN hypotheses are silent about label boundaries deliberately placed at escaping local parameters.
statements.consumer: The corrected compact-exhaustion theorem stops at a global lower bound and proves two-sided convergence only on expanding certified windows.

statements.justification: This question isolates the exact effective geometric package still needed to turn coherent recession operators into a finite globally honest search space.
statements.gap: The standing assumptions do not yet yield simultaneous canonical-section safety, collar compatibility, translated-uniform tails, or a refinement schedule whose total ledger vanishes.
statements.consumer: Only an affirmative answer, or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, can supply the finite Gaussian-rule premise needed by conditional CertGluePFL termination and replayable moving-offset certification.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct, or refute by a specific encoded experiment, a finite shared-trace recession library satisfying canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, simultaneous-collar compatibility, translated-uniform tails, and an input-computable refinement schedule with vanishing accumulated error.
obligation.obstruction: The available active-set geometry controls only forward motion from a fixed mean. It does not prove that canonical sections throughout protected stars preserve every active semantic region and the separated-risk set. Equality of shared mesh vertices on a geometric face does not control the actual face--cone candidates throughout simultaneous collar supports. No translated-uniform guard and normal-base tail bound or explicit refinement-count recurrence has been derived. Hence the standing assumptions currently support neither an affirmative construction nor a negative encoded-experiment witness.
obligation.attempted: The prior construction used one smoothed ancestor, one common rational simplicial fan, common raywise Følner factors, and shared finite-element face variables. This gives path-independent operators and explicit translation-boundary ratios. The proposed collar induction is circular if its traces are defined from the already-glued rule, while constant lower-skeleton extension can assign positive weight to an unsafe candidate. Per-cell bounds also cannot be summed without controlling the growing refinement count. In accordance with the directive after this barrier was isolated, no further generic averaging reroll was used.
obligation.partial_result:
Starting from the single ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\), \(\mathrm{lem:common\mbox{-}ray\mbox{-}folner\mbox{-}coherence}\) proves that, for every face inclusion \(\tau\preceq\sigma\),
\[
q_{\sigma,L}
=
\left(
\prod_{\varrho\in\mathscr R(\sigma)\setminus\mathscr R(\tau)}
\mathsf A_{\varrho,L}
\right)q_{\tau,L},
\]
independently of the incidence path, together with the bounds
\[
\left\|q_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-q_{\sigma,L}(w)\right\|_1
\leq 2\min\{1,a/L\}
\]
and
\[
\left|F^f_{\sigma,L}(w+a\varrho)-F^f_{\sigma,L}(w)\right|
\leq R_f\min\{1,a/L\}.
\]
The established smoothing, one-chart averaging, and weighted path results separately give
\[
R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\},
\qquad
\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\qquad
\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h)
\]
for each fixed finite library. These identities certify path-independent transitions and the stated componentwise errors only. They do not prove simultaneous safety on collar supports, tails uniform over translated means, or a refinement-count schedule whose accumulated ledger vanishes.

statements.statement:
Fix a rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\).  Let \(c_n,\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\) lie eventually in one fixed compact set \(C_c\subset\mathcal K_0\), suppose \(\|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\le\xi_n\), and define
\[
\chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n,
\qquad
A_0=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}
\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}.
\]
For any supplied Gaussian rule in the \(\widehat c_n\)-offset experiment and any supplied upper bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\ge\chi_n(C)\), the parameter-independent Carter and score transfer has semantic coverage discrepancy and normalized separated-risk discrepancy on \(C\) at most
\[
\Delta_n(C)=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
+\{H_C+2A_0\}\overline\chi_n(C),
\qquad H_C=H(C,C_c).
\]
The upper bound \(\overline\chi_n(C)\) is arbitrary and need not be effective.  If \(\overline\chi_n(C)\to0\), then \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).  This conclusion constructs no Gaussian rule and invokes no effective-compatible-density premise.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: exact affine-slack coupling, compact-offset finite-arrangement stability, and bounded Gaussian boundary density.}

For every active facet, \(\text{def:moving-slack-system}\) gives the exact identity
\[
\zeta_{n,j}(u)-\{\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u\}
=(c_{n,j}-\widehat c_{n,j})+e_{n,j}(u).
\tag{15}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\max_j\sup_{u\in C}
\left|\zeta_{n,j}(u)-\{\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u\}\right|
\le\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\le\chi_n(C).
\tag{16}
\]
The hypothesis that \(c_n\) and \(\widehat c_n\) lie in the same fixed compact \(C_c\subset\mathcal K_0\) is now used: it permits invocation of \(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) with its single finite constant
\(H_C=H(C,C_c)\).  Together with the centered score displacement \(d_n(C)\), (16) matches every completed semantic label mean and every separated-risk mean to the \(\widehat c_n\)-offset arrangement at Mahalanobis displacement at most
\[
H_C\chi_n(C).
\tag{17}
\]
The lemma's directed Hausdorff part handles rival semantic unions, and its equality convention retains all incident labels.

For each active \(j\), positivity of \(\Sigma_0\) and \(a_j\ne0\) imply \(a_j'\Sigma_0a_j>0\).  The same density calculation as in (12) gives, uniformly over the offset and the Gaussian mean,
\[
\Pr_h\{|c_j+a_j'W_0|\le s\}
\le\min\left\{1,
\frac{2s}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}\right\}.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak b_0(s)\le A_0s\).  In the moving-boundary comparison take the collar tolerance to be
\(\tau_n=\overline\chi_n(C)\).  Because
\(\chi_n(C)\le\overline\chi_n(C)\), the strict failure indicator
\(\mathbf1\{\chi_n(C)>\tau_n\}\) equals zero, while
\[
\mathfrak b_0\{\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\}
\le\mathfrak b_0\{2\overline\chi_n(C)\}
\le2A_0\overline\chi_n(C).
\tag{19}
\]
Also (17) is at most \(H_C\overline\chi_n(C)\).

By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), Carter's parameter-independent kernel contributes
\(C_{2/\kappa}|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|/\sqrt n\) on \(C\).  The affine score-normal replacement contributes \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\), and \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\) applies both to coverage indicators and to \(\ell_0\in[0,1]\).  Adding these nonnegative charges to (17)--(19) proves
\[
\Delta_n(C)
=C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}
+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
+(H_C+2A_0)\overline\chi_n(C).
\tag{20}
\]
If \(\overline\chi_n(C)\to0\), compactness of the fixed offset set keeps \(H_C\) fixed, \(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\to0\) by \(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\), and the Carter term vanishes.  Hence \(\Delta_n(C)\to0\).

statements.statement: The randomized-treatment, monotone-employment, always-employed model of Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes embeds in the present causal class only on the following restricted submodel: \(\mathcal X\) is a singleton; the known rational assignment probabilities satisfy \(\bar\pi_z\ge\pi_*\); \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\) almost surely; \(s=+1\); both potential wages take values in the finite grid \(\mathcal Y\); and, for \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\), \(P(EE)\ge m_*>0\).  On this restricted submodel the induced law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), every unit is a complier, the always-selected-complier event equals \(EE\), and \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\).  There is no inclusion of the unrestricted Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and their sharpness conclusion does not transfer automatically outside this restriction.
